item.title: Moyes insider doubts potential Celtic move - Tuesday's gossip
item.description: [Getty Images] Former striker Louis Saha, who played under David Moyes at Everton , doubts whether Celtic would be able to lure away the Premier League boss in their hunt to land a successor to Martin O'Neill. (Glasgow Times) Former Rangers striker Kris Boyd says manager Derek McInnes faces a big call on whether to restore forward Kevin Kelsy to his starting line-up on Saturday against St Johnstone . (Scottish Sun) Trabzonspor defender Stefan Savic believes his team can up the gears even more against Hearts after downing fierce rivals Besiktas on Monday. Mohamed Salah scored the second goal in the 2-0 win. (Daily Record) Dundee boss Steven Pressley faces an anxious wait as on-loan striker Bobby Wales has been sent to see a second specialist in a bid to get a definitive diagnosis on his ankle injury. (Daily Record) Jim Goodwin insists Dundee United were "desperate" to bring Amar Fatah back to Tannadice and made the player a handsome offer. (The Courier) Stephen Robinson says striker Ayoub Mouloua's ruthless Aberdeen impact in the win over St Mirren - after a week where he was only allowed to train on a static bike - has given him "food for thought". (Press and Journal) Kilmarnock manager Neil McCann stressed new signing Nico Mantl has a fight for the goalkeeper's jersey after Calum Ferrie delivered a big performance in Saturday's 3-2 win over Motherwell . (The Herald) Liverpool and Man Utd eye Nmecha - Tuesday's gossip Celtic target rejects new deal - Monday's gossip

item.title: UK's largest indoor tennis event returns to Wrexham
item.description: Wales' Mimi Xu won the 2025 Wrexham Open title [James Bayliss] The UK's largest indoor tennis event returns this week some of the biggest rising stars head to the Wrexham Open in search of glory. Among them is Armenia's Alina Charaeva, who made headlines by beating world number one Elena Rybakina in the China Open earlier this month. The 24-year-old also beat 2024 Wrexham Open winner Sonay Kartal at the China Open. The home crowd in Wrexham were treated to a Welsh winner in both the singles and doubles event in 2025, as Wales' Mimi Xu claimed both titles - alongside Ella McDonald. Xu will not be defending her titles, opting to compete at the W75 Saguenay tournament in Canada. This year Alicia Dudeney, Hannah Klugman and Junior Nationals champion Daniella Britton are among the British players seeking success in Wrexham. The number one seed is former top 40 player Anna Blinkova. Like Charaeva, the Russian-born French player has beaten Elena Rybakina - at the 2024 Australian Open. Other former top 50 players include Germany's Mona Barthel and Anna-Lena Friedsam, and Slovakian Rebecca Sramkova. The W100 ITF World Tennis Tour event takes place between 18-25 October, and is set to be the UK's biggest women's tournament outside of the grass-court season this year. item.title: 'It is just the beginning!' - Confident Omar Marmoush targets Tottenham resurgence after opening account in Coventry win
item.description: FBL-ENG-PR-TOTTENHAM-COVENTRY - AFP Egyptian forward inspires maiden victory Marmoush is confident his maiden strike for the Lilywhites during a 3-1 triumph over their newly-promoted visitors will spark a resurgence this term. Signed on loan from Manchester City , the attacker restored his side's lead in the 58th minute despite catching Milan van Ewijk in the face beforehand. That overdue win after three draws and three defeats lifts them from 20th to 16th. Returning playmaker sparks early dominance Returning playmaker sparks early dominance Fresh from a four-day warm-weather training camp in Marbella , the hosts broke the deadlock after 14 minutes through James Maddison, who converted Mohammed Kudus' pass against his boyhood club, Coventry. Although Dominic Solanke had an effort ruled out, Tottenham maintained control until Jan Paul van Hecke's turnover allowed Jack Rudoni to level after the restart. Marmoush subsequently struck before Ben Davies wrapped up the points in stoppage time. Speaking to BBC Sport after the final whistle, Marmoush expressed his delight over the victory and the team's overall display: "We are so, so happy. We have had good performances in that last week but haven't got the end result of a win. Very happy to win our first game today also happy to score my first goal for Tottenham. We will build on this." Discussing his maiden strike and how it felt to see his hard work secure maximum points, he added: "I am very happy it paid off but I am more happy for the three points we got today." Dressing room backs tactical blueprint An encouraging night for Roberto De Zerbi's side was further boosted when Dejan Kulusevski made his first appearance since recovering from a serious knee injury that ruled him out of the entire previous campaign. At the back, the hosts successfully thwarted early threats from Frank Lampard's visiting Coventry outfit. Reflecting on the team's ongoing development and addressing the threat posed by their opponents, Marmoush said: "I mean every game we learn. As you said we've played amazing in the first few weeks but the result wasn't there. It is just the beginning." He also praised the quality of their visitors while acknowledging the importance of Davies' strike: "They're a very good team, good on transitions. Ben's goal got us the three points and got the game to clam down." Highlighting the positive impact of his head coach and the strong unity within the squad, the forward added: "Yeah I feel amazing. With the coach, he helps us all and teaches us small details. He also helps us on a personal basis. I love the intensity and passion that he brings. We believe in the system that we play in. On the pitch we are like a big family and we will fight for each other until the end." Fresh injury concerns cloud celebration Fresh injury concerns cloud celebration Despite ending their winless start, Tottenham's medical staff must now assess fresh knocks sustained by defenders Robertson and Tosin Adarabioyo. item.title: Liverpool could be set to battle Man United in the race for Bundesliga star
item.description: Liverpool could be set to battle Man United in the race for Bundesliga star Liverpool and Manchester United Tracking Felix Nmecha as Borussia Dortmund Hold Firm on £84m Valuation Liverpool are among the Premier League clubs keeping close tabs on Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha, with TeamTalk reporting that Manchester United are also firmly in the mix for the Germany international. Nmecha, 26, continues to build a strong profile in the Bundesliga and his situation is drawing growing attention in England. The report states that Manchester United have shown concrete intent, having “maintained a persistent interest in Nmecha” and are “understood to have made contact as they assess options ahead of the winter window.” Liverpool’s interest appears more conditional, but still significant. Nmecha has “emerged as one potential alternative should their pursuit of Bournemouth’s Alex Scott prove fruitless”, which places him squarely on the club’s radar as recruitment planning continues. Felix Nmecha interest gathers pace Nmecha’s appeal is easy to understand. He has top-level experience, tactical flexibility and a profile suited to the modern Premier League game. As TeamTalk notes, his “performances for club and country have strengthened his reputation as a versatile, energetic central midfielder capable of contributing in both boxes.” Photo: IMAGO There is also a strong English connection. Born in Hamburg, Nmecha spent more than a decade in Manchester City’s academy before forging his senior reputation with Wolfsburg and Borussia Dortmund. That background, combined with his development in Germany, gives him a blend of technical quality and physical maturity that many elite clubs value highly. Borussia Dortmund set £84m marker Dortmund’s stance is the major obstacle. The Bundesliga club are in a strong negotiating position after Nmecha signed a contract extension until June 2030 earlier this year. According to the report, “there is no active release clause that can be triggered in January”, with an €80million clause only becoming active from the summer of 2027. For now, Dortmund are holding out for much more. Their valuation is said to be “in the region of €90-100million”, putting the upper end at around £84.2m. That is a significant outlay for any club, especially for a player whose current side have no need to sell. The messaging from Germany is equally clear. Dortmund’s sporting director, Ole Book, has “previously played down the prospect of a departure, describing a sale as highly unlikely.” With Nmecha central under Niko Kovač and a regular starter, “the 26-year-old is expected to remain at Signal Iduna Park” for the time being. Liverpool transfer plans may hinge on midfield priorities Timing will be crucial. TeamTalk indicates that “any realistic move is more likely to materialise in at the end of the season not in the coming weeks.” That matters for Liverpool, who will weigh need, value and competition before making any decisive push. The report states that Manchester United have shown concrete intent, having “maintained a persistent interest in Nmecha” and are “understood to have made contact as they assess options ahead of the winter window.” Liverpool’s interest appears more conditional, but still significant. Nmecha has “emerged as one potential alternative should their pursuit of Bournemouth’s Alex Scott prove fruitless”, which places him squarely on the club’s radar as recruitment planning continues. Felix Nmecha interest gathers pace Nmecha’s appeal is easy to understand. He has top-level experience, tactical flexibility and a profile suited to the modern Premier League game. As TeamTalk notes, his “performances for club and country have strengthened his reputation as a versatile, energetic central midfielder capable of contributing in both boxes.” Photo: IMAGO There is also a strong English connection. Born in Hamburg, Nmecha spent more than a decade in Manchester City’s academy before forging his senior reputation with Wolfsburg and Borussia Dortmund. That background, combined with his development in Germany, gives him a blend of technical quality and physical maturity that many elite clubs value highly. Borussia Dortmund set £84m marker Dortmund’s stance is the major obstacle. The Bundesliga club are in a strong negotiating position after Nmecha signed a contract extension until June 2030 earlier this year. According to the report, “there is no active release clause that can be triggered in January”, with an €80million clause only becoming active from the summer of 2027. For now, Dortmund are holding out for much more. Their valuation is said to be “in the region of €90-100million”, putting the upper end at around £84.2m. That is a significant outlay for any club, especially for a player whose current side have no need to sell. The messaging from Germany is equally clear. Dortmund’s sporting director, Ole Book, has “previously played down the prospect of a departure, describing a sale as highly unlikely.” With Nmecha central under Niko Kovač and a regular starter, “the 26-year-old is expected to remain at Signal Iduna Park” for the time being. Liverpool transfer plans may hinge on midfield priorities Timing will be crucial. TeamTalk indicates that “any realistic move is more likely to materialise in at the end of the season not in the coming weeks.” That matters for Liverpool, who will weigh need, value and competition before making any decisive push. If Alex Scott proves unattainable, Nmecha could become a more serious consideration. Yet at up to £84m, this feels like a transfer that would require absolute conviction, not merely admiration from afar. Our View This is the sort of link that immediately grabs attention because Felix Nmecha does look like a Liverpool midfielder on paper. He covers ground, carries the ball well and has the kind of athletic presence that can raise the level of a midfield unit over a long season. If the club are genuinely looking at alternatives to Alex Scott, it suggests there is a clear profile being targeted rather than a random list of names. The fee is where the intrigue turns into hesitation. Up to £84m is a huge number, especially for a player who, while talented, would still arrive with pressure attached from day one. Liverpool have generally wanted certainty when spending at that level, and Dortmund know exactly how to protect their best assets. With no January release clause and a contract to 2030, they hold every card. There is also the Manchester United angle, which always sharpens the story. If both clubs are watching closely, the race becomes louder very quickly, even if no move is imminent. It feels more like groundwork than a deal on the brink. Still, this is one to keep in mind. If Liverpool decide they need a dynamic all-round midfielder and other routes close off, Nmecha has enough quality to become far more than a fallback option.

item.title: What Commanders’ Dan Quinn said about crucial fourth-down play vs. 49ers
item.description: So, we’ve all seen it. And it was weird. The video on the ESPN broadcast feed from Monday night’s game between the Commanders and 49ers showed what looked like Washington head coach Dan Quinn saying something that amounts to the fact he was unsure of what down it was. That’s a rough look after the game management nightmare that resulted in a tie with the New York Giants in Week 5. Quinn couldn’t afford one in Week 6. One was (apparently) was caught on camera. Or maybe not. Either way, it looked, well, not great. The Commanders head coach says this is much ado about nothing , but let’s rewind. Washington had a fourth-and-2 with roughly 13 minutes left in the second quarter. Jayden Daniels rolled to his right and then a flag fell down, though the play was allowed to complete. The quarterback inexplicably threw the ball out of bounds and to no one. Did Jayden Daniels just throw the ball away on 4th down??? #NFL #Commanders #RaiseHail #49ers #FTTB #WASvsSF pic.twitter.com/WzU2IxfkeF — Dom (@ZeroChillSports) October 20, 2026 That’s a curious decision in itself, to say the least. Why wouldn’t you put the ball in play and try to convert? Even more trouble was this the video you’ll view below, where it looks like Dan Quinn didn’t know what down it was. Here’s his explanation of that issue , as told to on-site reporters during his Monday postgame press conference . "I definitely knew it was 4th down." Commanders HC Dan Quinn on the 4th down play that Jayden Daniels threw the ball away in the second quarter. pic.twitter.com/SiBP2SIClg — ESPN (@espn) October 20, 2026 “I definitely knew it was fourth down,” Quinn said. “We were going for it. And, what I think you’re referring to, with the illegal shift there’s not a penalty to go for a field goal. It’s a turnover on downs.” After the game-management kerfuffle from a week ago, that’s a good thing. And it still wasn’t a great look. The 49ers declined the flag, negating that point, and locking in a turnover on downs. No matter what actually happened on the headset, the result was a major disappointment considering the ball was on the 49ers 13-yard line. The Commanders simply must’ve come up with a score there and they didn’t. That led to trouble at the end of the game that the Commanders ultimately lost. Success on the play we’re talking about could’ve changed the game. There's no way Dan Quinn's saying "Aww, that was 4th down" like people are suggesting? There's no way, right? I refuse to believe that. pic.twitter.com/37ZoU64cFK — Grant Paulsen (@GrantPaulsen) October 20, 2026 The Commanders ultimately fell just short, and all these little moment matter. Do you think Dan Quinn knew it was fourth down? Let us know in the article comments below. It’s 2:30 a.m. when I’m writing this. I’m very tired. Please excuse the typos that are most certainly in this story. — SB

Fantasy football managers entering Week 7 face a quarterback landscape shaped by rising stars, resurgent veterans, and injury concerns that could change the starting picture before kickoff. The key this week is balancing recent form with matchup potential while keeping a close eye on late-week injury reports. Here are the top quarterback picks and sleepers to consider as the 2026 NFL regular season continues. Week 7 Top Fantasy Football Picks Brock Purdy , SF (@ ATL) Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Brock Purdy remains an attractive fantasy football starter heading into Week 7 , particularly with a favorable matchup against the Atlanta Falcons. The San Francisco 49ers quarterback completed 19 of 29 passes for 189 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in Week 6. Purdy benefited from two early turnovers that gave San Francisco short fields. He also connected several times with Mike Evans late in the game. Although he was sacked three times, his overall performance helped the 49ers secure an important divisional win. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) His passing yardage was modest, but fantasy managers should not overlook his touchdown production. The matchup against Atlanta gives him a chance to deliver a more complete statistical performance. After throwing seven interceptions during his first four games, Maye has now completed two consecutive games without a turnover. A Week 7 matchup against the Chicago Bears offers another opportunity to build on that momentum. He offers a combination of established production and touchdown potential. Week 7 Fantasy Football Sleepers Tyler Shough, NO (vs. PIT) Tyler Shough is an intriguing streaming candidate. That’s after helping New Orleans defeat the Giants 34-27. He completed 16 of 30 passes for 144 yards and three touchdowns, then added another score on the ground. His passing yardage was limited, but the four total touchdowns made the performance valuable for fantasy football managers. A matchup against Pittsburgh awaits in Week 7. Shough carries risk because of his injury and modest passing totals. Still, his ability to generate touchdowns gives him streaming appeal. Shough is a high-upside option for deeper leagues, provided his hand does not limit his availability or effectiveness. However, his yardage and scoring production made the outing encouraging. The interception remains a concern, but his ability to surpass 300 passing yards demonstrates great upside. Cousins is a viable streamer for managers seeking passing volume and a potential multi-touchdown performance. Aaron Rodgers, PIT (@ NO) Morgan Tencza-Imagn Images. Rodgers connected repeatedly with DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard, targeting each 11 times. That concentration of passing opportunities could help him maintain fantasy football relevance against New Orleans. Rodgers is a reasonable streaming option, especially in deeper leagues where dependable alternatives are limited. Jalen Hurts is reportedly expected to miss the rest of the season because of blood clots. That makes alternative quarterback plans especially important for his fantasy football managers. item.title: Deadline Passes With No Contract Extensions For Indiana Pacers Players
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 02: Jarace Walker #5 and Ben Sheppard #26 of the Indiana Pacers pose for photos during Indiana Pacers Media Day at Ascension St Vincent Center on October 02, 2023 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) Getty Images INDIANAPOLIS – Monday, NBA teams faced two deadlines related to contract extensions. 6 p.m. ET was the last minute that teams could sign players in the final year of their rookie-scale contracts to a contract extension while 11:59 p.m. ET was the cutoff for players who have multiple years remaining on their deals to be extended – if eligible, of course. Those deadlines created action around the league with the likes of Cason Wallace (Oklahoma City Thunder), Oso Ighodaro (Phoenix Suns), Jaden McDaniels (Minnesota Timberwolves), and Brandon Miller (Charlotte Hornets) adding years, and money, to their contracts on Monday. Wallace and Miller inked rookie-scale extensions while Ighodaro and McDaniels signed veteran extensions. The Indiana Pacers were a team worth keeping an eye on with those time limits in mind. They have two players, Ben Sheppard and Jarace Walker, currently in the final year of their rookie-scale deals. They were both eligible for five-year extensions. The Pacers also had several veterans with multiple years remaining on their contract who were extension eligible until midnight on Monday – that list included Pascal Siakam, Tyrese Haliburton, Obi Toppin, T.J. McConnell, Ivica Zubac, and Andrew Nembhard. With over half of their roster extension eligible, the Pacers had a lot to consider. General manager Chad Buchanan didn’t offer insight into the team’s thinking when asked about possible contract extensions last month. “We do have a lot of guys that are in that boat. We’ll keep that to ourselves on that one,” he said. Last year, the Pacers agreed to terms on a new deal with wing Aaron Nesmith about two hours before the deadline to do so. They have been proactive with contract extensions when applicable. This offseason came with a different result. None of the eight extension-eligible Pacers players who were facing a deadline on Monday agreed to terms on an extension . They will all go through the 2026-27 season without any changes being possible for their contracts. For Walker and Sheppard, that means free agency is coming in 2027. They could be restricted free agents if they are sent a qualifying offer next summer, but it’s too early to determine their specific free agency status – both players will be looking for a new contract if they are restricted or unrestricted. Siakam, Toppin, Nembhard, and Zubac will now all enter the 2027 offseason with just one year remaining on their deals. They will all be extension eligible again next summer and will remain eligible for one throughout the 2027-28 season. “They (his agents) do that for me. I focus on basketball... I’m not really worried about that,” Siakam said earlier this month when asked about a possible extension. Minne
item.content:encoded: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 02: Jarace Walker #5 and Ben Sheppard #26 of the Indiana Pacers pose for photos during Indiana Pacers Media Day at Ascension St Vincent Center on October 02, 2023 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) Getty Images INDIANAPOLIS – Monday, NBA teams faced two deadlines related to contract extensions. 6 p.m. ET was the last minute that teams could sign players in the final year of their rookie-scale contracts to a contract extension while 11:59 p.m. ET was the cutoff for players who have multiple years remaining on their deals to be extended – if eligible, of course. Those deadlines created action around the league with the likes of Cason Wallace (Oklahoma City Thunder), Oso Ighodaro (Phoenix Suns), Jaden McDaniels (Minnesota Timberwolves), and Brandon Miller (Charlotte Hornets) adding years, and money, to their contracts on Monday. Wallace and Miller inked rookie-scale extensions while Ighodaro and McDaniels signed veteran extensions. The Indiana Pacers were a team worth keeping an eye on with those time limits in mind. They have two players, Ben Sheppard and Jarace Walker, currently in the final year of their rookie-scale deals. They were both eligible for five-year extensions. The Pacers also had several veterans with multiple years remaining on their contract who were extension eligible until midnight on Monday – that list included Pascal Siakam, Tyrese Haliburton, Obi Toppin, T.J. McConnell, Ivica Zubac, and Andrew Nembhard. With over half of their roster extension eligible, the Pacers had a lot to consider. General manager Chad Buchanan didn’t offer insight into the team’s thinking when asked about possible contract extensions last month. “We do have a lot of guys that are in that boat. We’ll keep that to ourselves on that one,” he said. Last year, the Pacers agreed to terms on a new deal with wing Aaron Nesmith about two hours before the deadline to do so. They have been proactive with contract extensions when applicable. This offseason came with a different result. None of the eight extension-eligible Pacers players who were facing a deadline on Monday agreed to terms on an extension . They will all go through the 2026-27 season without any changes being possible for their contracts. For Walker and Sheppard, that means free agency is coming in 2027. They could be restricted free agents if they are sent a qualifying offer next summer, but it’s too early to determine their specific free agency status – both players will be looking for a new contract if they are restricted or unrestricted. Siakam, Toppin, Nembhard, and Zubac will now all enter the 2027 offseason with just one year remaining on their deals. They will all be extension eligible again next summer and will remain eligible for one throughout the 2027-28 season. “They (his agents) do that for me. I focus on basketball... I’m not really worried about that,” Siakam said earlier this month when asked about a possible extension. Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball, center, passes between Indiana Pacers forward Pascal Siakam (43) and center Ivica Zubac (40) during the first half of a preseason NBA basketball game, Wednesday, Oct. 7, 2026, in Ames, Iowa. (AP Photo/Charlie Neibergall) Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. McConnell and Haliburton will both still have two years left on their agreements in 2027. They both have different considerations at play – Haliburton would become eligible for a supermax contract if he makes an All-NBA team or wins either MVP or Defensive Player of the Year in the next three seasons. McConnell’s contract is only partially guaranteed in 2027-28 and has a team option covering the 2028-29 campaign. Did any extensions make sense for the Pacers on Monday? The Pacers are over the luxury tax line for the ongoing season and approaching the first apron. While Sheppard and Walker are on expiring contracts, Nesmith gets a big raise next season while many players will see a smaller bump in salary. Indiana is a good team and, naturally, expensive. That makes contract extensions, especially ones that come while a player has multiple seasons left on their current deal, less likely by default. The Pacers need to be certain with their spending going forward as they look to keep contending during Haliburton’s prime. Every contract is important in the apron-era of the NBA. While contract extensions can make sense for any number of reasons, the general uncertainty for Indiana entering the coming campaign adds to the risk that comes with longer deals. While the team had a strong, confidence-building preseason, they still need to see Haliburton get through the schedule after a torn Achilles caused him to miss all of last season. Zubac is adjusting to the team’s system. Newcomers Kelly Oubre and Larry Nance have to prove they can help the team once they are on their opponent’s scouting reports with more detail. Is the Pacers depth good enough? Will they need more at any specific position? That those are questions at all makes having flexibility valuable, and the Pacers kept themselves nimble by not extending any contracts on Monday. Siakam, Zubac, and Nembhard stood out as candidates for a longer deal. But ultimately, the Pacers agreed to no new deals ahead of the 2026-27 season. In theory, Jay Huff (in just over one week) and Johnny Furphy could get a contract extension mid-season if their team options for 2027-28 are declined. But that feels exceedingly unlikely for both players at this moment. It’s time for basketball to be the Pacers’ focus. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: Cristante hints at imminent return from injury: “We’re almost there.”
item.description: Cristante hints at imminent return from injury: “We’re almost there.” Bryan Cristante finally sees the end of the tunnel. “I’m fine, we’re almost there.” Few words, but enough to raise Roma’s hopes. The Giallorossi midfielder reassured reporters at Trigoria yesterday during the fifteen-minute training session open to the press, hinting that his return to the group is now imminent. As reported by Il Corriere dello Sport, Cristante underwent another personalized session, still with a large bandage on his right knee. The good news is that the inflammation is no longer causing pain. Before the final training session, the player also spoke with Gian Piero Gasperini. Cristante’s return could come as early as the match against Napoli. Gasperini himself, in the pre-match press conference, hinted at the possibility: “We hope he can play in Naples, or at least be available.” The midfielder will therefore also miss tonight’s match against Slovan Bratislava, after already missing the matches against Como, Real Madrid, and Genoa. However, his condition is improving, and the Giallorossi staff hopes to have him available for the next league match.

item.title: Emotional James Maddison scores dream goal on first competitive start in 536 days as Tottenham finally clinch first league win
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur v Coventry City - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Maddison makes immediate impact on return Maddison enjoyed a fairytale return to the Tottenham starting lineup, marking his first start in 536 days with a goal that set the tone for a crucial victory . The England playmaker, who has battled back from consecutive knee ligament injuries, needed only 14 minutes to make his presence felt. He produced a delicate first-time finish that looped over goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, promptly celebrating with his iconic darts-inspired gesture to the home crowd. The goal was his first since a Europa League semi-final against Bodo/Glimt in the 2024-25 season. Maddison reflected on the significance of his contribution after the final whistle. "They're the ones you dream of. Without going too deep into it, them dark days last year, recovering from the ACL, you dream of them moments, them goals and that is the light at the end of the tunnel," he told Sky Sports . Double injury boost for De Zerbi Double injury boost for De Zerbi While Maddison provided the inspiration, the match also marked a momentous return for Dejan Kulusevski. The Swedish international was introduced as a second-half substitute, ending a gruelling 17-month period out of action due to injury. His arrival onto the pitch was met with a standing ovation, providing a psychological lift for a Tottenham side that had seen Omar Marmoush restore their lead in the 58th minute before three players were forced off with fitness concerns. Maddison admitted he felt a strong connection to his teammate’s struggle, stating: "That is why I was a bit emotional and I felt really proud of Dejan Kulusevski as well because him coming back. I knew exactly that feeling of him stepping onto the pitch after that time out, but those moments and goals make it all worth it." Tactical talks pay off for Spurs The decision to start Maddison was a calculated move by De Zerbi, who has been cautious with the player's integration after a fragmented start to the season. Maddison revealed that he had proactively sought a starting role, believing the time was right to test his fitness in a competitive environment. The playmaker expressed his gratitude for the manager's faith, noting that he wanted to remind the supporters and the staff of the quality he brings to the engine room. "I spoke to the gaffer about it this week and just feeling like the right moment for me to go back into the starting XI after a stop-start start to the season. I just wanted to play well, show my quality and show what the team's missed in the last 18 months, or whatever it is since my last start. The gaffer asked me to play and said he wanted to enjoy watching me from the side so hopefully I did that," Maddison explained. Having entered the fixture languishing rock bottom of the table, this crucial victory propels them up to 16th place, pulling level on six points with Coventry and edging ahead of their opponents on goal difference. Now, their primary objective will be to sustain this newfound momentum and build upon the triumph as they prepare to visit Stamford Bridge for a high-stakes clash against London rivals Chelsea.

item.title: Ex-WWE Referee Raves About Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling’s Potential
item.description: Ex-WWE Referee Praises MLP Getty Former WWE referee Jimmy Korderas shared high praise for Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling (MLP). Korderas believes MLP has a strong foundation can has the potential for continued growth. MLP is a Canadian-based pro wrestling company founded by Scott D’Amore. The company has quickly established itself, particularly through its media rights deal with TSN. TSN is one of Canada’s biggest and most historic networks, giving the company a platform to succeed. MLP’s show Mayhem aired on TSN, and MyAEW, thanks to the company’s working relationship with Tony Khan’s AEW. Korderas praised MLP’s production value and in-ring talent. He feels that the company can establish itself as the premier destination for pro wrestling in Canada. Ex-WWE Referee Jimmy Korderas Raves About MLP’s Potential Jimmy Korderas raved about MLP’s potential as a pro wrestling company. The roster consists of a mix of independent wrestlers, local Canadian talent, and AEW stars. At MLP Northern Rising earlier this month, AEW stars Adam Copeland and Andrade El Idolo were among the wrestlers featured. The event took place at Mattamy Athletic Centre, formerly known as Maple Leaf Gardens, an iconic venue. Mattamy Athletic Centre could become a regular venue for MLP’s biggest events, further helping to establish the company. While the partnership with AEW is positive, Korderas believes the best is still yet to come for MLP. “[MLP], who are a growing company, I think they have something there. They have a product that I think can grow into something much bigger, at least in Canada, if not further on, because they are on the MyAEW platform now too. So [fans] can see it everywhere. And it is a good product,” Korderas told The Game Plan . He added: “It is different. I think it’s a different presentation from what everybody else is doing because they have a nice mix of talent.” Korderas Weighs In on MLP’s Production Korderas also shared his thoughts on MLP’s production, saying that it is very impressive for such a new company. The former WWE referee noted that Scott D’Amore’s company has established its own identity. “They have a nice mix of how they present their wrestling on television. It’s not as produced as WWE, nobody is. I mean, they’re different from everybody else. AEW is more wrestling focused, like in-ring focused than anything else,” Korderas told The Game Plan . “That’s where MLP is different, where they do a little bit of everything. Because back when Vince McMahon used to say – and I know people hated this – was, ‘We’re a variety show. We have a little bit of everything for everyone'” “If you concentrate on one single niche audience, then you’re missing out on a whole bunch of people watching your product and enjoying it,” he said. “You can do comedy? There’s a place for comedy. There’s a place for hardcore, a place for straight up wrestling.” He continued: “I think that’s what MLP’s bread and butter is right now, is they’re a nice mix. And using social medi

item.title: Rays’ Yandy Diaz celebrates ALCS win with massive Tomahawk steak
item.description: Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Rays’ Yandy Diaz celebrates ALCS win with massive Tomahawk steak appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tampa Bay Rays beat the Cleveland Guardians 7-3 in Game 6 of the ACLS, clinching a World Series berth and eliciting a confident take for the final round from manager Kevin Cash . Rays pitcher Freddy Peralta described his journey following a trade that helped him punch the World Series tickets of his teammates, including emotional leader and DH Yandy Diaz. Diaz once again found himself in the limelight after the Game 6, as he was seen eating a large hunk of meat reserved for the grandest of celebrations: a tomahawk steak that looked straight out of the Medieval Times restaurant and dinner show chain. He happily chowed down on the steak while flexing for the cameras as he put on a show for Rays fans everywhere. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Yandy Diaz is once again consuming a celebratory tomahawk steak pic.twitter.com/jZyMmg2Iiq — Talkin' Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) October 20, 2026 The Rays got two runs in the second inning and one in the third inning as they began to chip away at a patchwork Guardians pitching staff led by Tim Herrin, Cade Smith and Shawn Armstrong. The Guardians’ dam began to spring a leak in the seventh inning as Junior Caminero went deep off the left-field foul pole, a two-run shot that had fans dancing in the aisles at Tropicana Stadium in St. Petersburg, Florida. Diaz had a home run, a run scored and two runs batted in on the night as Cash’s lineup showed its resolve and strength in a winning effort. The Rays slugger appeared to predict a World Series championship through a translator after the game as he celebrated with teammates. He will almost certainly be well-fed, and well-rested enough, as the Fall Classic opens up on October 23 at American Family Field in Milwaukee. Related: Why the Rays don’t have what it takes to beat Brewers in the World Series Related: Freddy Peralta’s wild run with Rays is like no other since 1968

The Warriors defeated the Lakers 101-89. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) Getty The Golden State Warriors will open the 2026-27 season on the road at Crypto.com Arena against the Los Angeles Lakers on October 21. item.title: Totti: “Friedkins have other plans, but if Roma need me…”
item.description: Totti: “Friedkins have other plans, but if Roma need me…” Francesco Totti presented his new book, “Oltre.” Vincent Candela, Max Biagi, Noemi Bocchi, his children, and Gian Piero Gasperini were present to witness the event. “Over these 50 years, I have given and received so much love, especially from my family, my children, and the people. It was a simple, beautiful, transparent give and take. I think this is the most important thing for me. I was doing a job I’ve always wanted, a passion of mine, and something I enjoy,” he said from the stage of the Teatro Brancaccio. The former Roma captain continued: “I’ve always tried to give and convey what I felt when I played football. For me, this was true love; it’s not easy to transform what you think. In those moments, I was sure of myself, and I hope that the love I had inside reached people.” Then Francesco returned to his farewell to football: “I’m dead, from a certain point of view. It was a forced moment, a forced farewell. One that I didn’t want and didn’t feel. I knew that sooner or later it had to happen, because everything has a beginning and an end. But for me it was painful in this case, different from how I had thought. In the end, I think it’s the norm in a job like football, where when you’re useful, you’re useful and when you’re not useful, you’re no longer useful. It’s a wrong way of thinking, but unfortunately it’s the truth.” After hanging up his boots he was ‘scared’: “I miss those 2-3 things I was used to doing every day. If you take the ground from under us, we start to wobble. Since it wasn’t my will, but it was all in a rush and suddenly, seeing as I was the last to know about it, I reluctantly accepted. I accepted the management’s decision and, as I said, ‘I’m scared’. I didn’t know what I would find by turning the page, what I wanted. I’m a very sensitive person, quite often I withdraw into myself and don’t express myself. A quality, a flaw, I don’t know. At the same time, I went over all 25 years thinking about the good and bad things, if I had made mistakes with certain people lately. I couldn’t understand what was happening, I felt lost. ‘Dead’ is a heavy word, but when a 25-year journey and such an important history with a single shirt ends… I said ‘I’m scared’”. During the evening, Gian Piero Gasperini also spoke via video call, receiving a prolonged round of applause from those in attendance. Totti was the first to speak, thanking the coach for bringing Roma back to the Champions League: “This is thanks to you, for giving us the chance to relive those magical nights that Roma deserves to see and play in. Roma deserves that stage, and thanks to you for bringing us back there.” Gasperini reciprocated the affection, returning to the match against Real Madrid: “The most beautiful spectacle the other night was the stadium. It was a great match, but seeing so much enthusiasm in this city was truly moving. I’m sorry I can’t be there tonight, but I wanted to be there somehow.” Tot

If you take the ground from under us, we start to wobble. Since it wasn’t my will, but it was all in a rush and suddenly, seeing as I was the last to know about it, I reluctantly accepted. I accepted the management’s decision and, as I said, ‘I’m scared’. I didn’t know what I would find by turning the page, what I wanted. I couldn’t understand what was happening, I felt lost. ‘Dead’ is a heavy word, but when a 25-year journey and such an important history with a single shirt ends… I said ‘I’m scared’”. During the evening, Gian Piero Gasperini also spoke via video call, receiving a prolonged round of applause from those in attendance. Totti was the first to speak, thanking the coach for bringing Roma back to the Champions League: “This is thanks to you, for giving us the chance to relive those magical nights that Roma deserves to see and play in. Roma deserves that stage, and thanks to you for bringing us back there.” Gasperini reciprocated the affection, returning to the match against Real Madrid: “The most beautiful spectacle the other night was the stadium. It was a great match, but seeing so much enthusiasm in this city was truly moving. I’m sorry I can’t be there tonight, but I wanted to be there somehow.” Totti didn’t rule out attending the Olimpico for Roma vs. Slovan Bratislava: “Okay, if I find tickets, I’ll come.” Asked about the Giallorossi’s Scudetto ambitions, after the resounding “no” from the crowd, the number 10 preferred to temper his enthusiasm: “Let’s focus on tomorrow.” A reference to the future and the possibility of seeing Totti back at Roma was also inevitable, a return that has been talked about for years but has never materialized. The former captain made no secret of his differences with the owners: “Usually, when you meet, it’s a two-way meeting, not a one-on-one. In seven or eight years, it’s never happened. You can see that the other side doesn’t have the same thoughts, the same ideas. They have different ideas about life, thought, and work. But that’s the way it should be, I’m happy to accept it. Either we do things together, or we don’t do them at all. If the other side isn’t willing or doesn’t have the same thoughts as me, let’s stop here. We don’t have to go ‘any further,’ it seems like the right thing to do.” A door that, at least for now, remains closed, without however damaging the bond with the Giallorossi colors. Totti concluded with a wish for the owners and a promise of love for his Roma: “I hope the Friedkins go as far as possible. I’m behind the scenes, but I’m always there for Roma.”

item.title: Stevenson 'granted' Zuffa release without fighting
item.description: Shakur Stevenson is unbeaten in 25 professional fights [Getty Images] Shakur Stevenson says he has secured a release from Zuffa Boxing without fighting for the promotion. Multiple-weight world champion Stevenson, 29, was one of several high-profile signings for the Saudi Arabian-backed boxing promotion headed by UFC owners TKO and Dana White. He was in talks to fight WBO welterweight champion Devin Haney but those discussions appear to have broken down – with Stevenson saying he was now a "free agent". "I requested to be released from Zuffa Boxing," Stevenson said on his Youtube channel. "Now, over the weekend, my request has been granted." Zuffa Boxing has not comment on Stevenson's suggested exit from the promotion. White has vowed to take over boxing and his most eye-catching signing was that of Conor Benn, poaching the Briton from Matchroom and Eddie Hearn. Benn has now had two fights with Zuffa, the second being last month's quick knockout defeat by world champion Ryan Garcia. Stevenson's last outing was an impressive win against American rival Teofimo Lopez, when he became a four-weight world champion. The New Jersey native was keen to be become a five-weight world champion by fighting Haney, but Stevenson says he has been left frustrated by being on the sidelines since signing with Zuffa in July. "I've been in camp for like eight weeks, preparing for fights that I was told was going to happen and have not happened," Stevenson said. "It is what it is. This is the business of boxing. I'm not mad at anyone, I'm not pointing fingers. "I am taking my career in my own hands and starting my own promotional company and I'm willing to work with other promoters and anybody else that's willing to be as serious about my career as I am," he added. Stevenson says he now plans to defend his WBO light-welterweight world title before moving up to welterweight in the coming years. item.title: Reese stars as Dream win first WNBA Finals match
item.description: Atlanta Dream are making their first appearance in the WNBA Finals since 2013, while Golden State Valkyries are making their debut after playing their first season in 2025 [Getty Images] Atlanta Dream won their first ever game in the WNBA Finals as they beat the Golden State Valkyries 79-65 to level the series at 1-1. Angel Reese scored 30 points and grabbed 16 rebounds as the Dream condemned the Valkyries to a defeat in front of their fans in San Francisco. The Georgia franchise held a 39-37 half-time lead and took control of the match in a 13-minute spell spanning the third and fourth quarter, adding 30 points while only conceding eight in return. Reese scored nine of her points in that period and becomes only the third player to reach 30 points and 15 rebounds in a Finals series, following Jonquel Jones in 2019 and Breanna Stewart in 2020. The 24-year-old, who is in her first season with the Dream after being traded from the Chicago Sky, is also the youngest player to reach the landmark in a WNBA post-season match. "She just came out on a mission tonight," said defensive guard Allisha Gray of her team-mate. The Dream had lost the match of the series 68-64 on Saturday, and Reese - the league's defensive player of the year - said she was keen to make amends for her performance in that game. "I let my team down last game, not really contributing as much as I could in the second half," said Reese. "I just wanted to make sure I came out tonight and left my mark. And I think I did that. "I was hungry, I think we let one slip away [on Saturday]. You can't do that. We felt disappointed, we felt embarrassed. "I walked off the court not feeling like myself, and I wanted to make sure that, this game, I did everything I could do to walk off the court and feel like who I am." The Dream had previously had a record of zero wins and 10 defeats in the Finals, following 3-0 series defeats in 2010, 2011 and 2013. After two matches in California, the best-of-seven series now switches to Atlanta, where games three and four will be played on Thursday, 22 October and Saturday, 24 October.

item.title: Liverpool given green light to bring £75m star to Anfield soon
item.description: Liverpool given green light to bring £75m star to Anfield soon Andoni Iraola may have lost Liverpool's unbeaten streak in the Premier League a couple of weeks ago but, that doesn't mean that they can stop trying. Now that most of the Premier League's fixtures from game week seven are done, the Reds have more of an idea about where they're sitting in the table. At the moment, they're fifth in the league and, while this may seem good from an outside perspective, the fact that they've only bagged nine goals across their entire Premier League campaign so far is worrying. By comparison, all four teams ahead of them in the table have score many more goals. This lack of form has led to many different transfer rumours being shared and now, the Anfield outfit have seemingly been given the green light to get one deal over the line. Felix Nmecha would happily return to England amid Liverpool's interest Liverpool's midfield is still their main problem area . The Anfield outfit only have four options among their ranks to choose from as their defensive midfielders and, while some of their performances have been solid, they've mostly left a lot to be desired. Trey Nyoni and Alexis Mac Allister have been their two best central midfielders thus far which, after giving Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch bumper new deals, is rather worrying. Even though some players such as Szoboszlai performed really well last term, they've failed to meet expectations this time around which has caused others such as Adam Wharton, Lamine Camara and Alex Scott to all be linked . However, as per a fresh update from Caught Offside, Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha could be the player they end up targeting instead, that is, especially since he's now open to making a return to England. "That player is Borussia Dortmund’s Felix Nmecha, who was also linked with Liverpool and other Premier League clubs during the summer," they wrote . "And as I reported back in January, Nmecha ended up signing a new contract with Dortmund. This, however, has not put off Liverpool, who are keeping a close eye on the Germany international in case they can’t get a deal done for Scott. "Nmecha would be cheaper and looks like good value in an inflated market. Recruitment staff inside Anfield see him as an underrated gem who could immediately make an impact in Andoni Iraola’s side. "Nmecha is understood to be open to coming back to English football after spending 12 years in Manchester City’s academy between 2007 and 2019. item.title: Wesley: United step up interest in AS Roma ace ahead of January window
item.description: Wesley: United step up interest in AS Roma ace ahead of January window Manchester United are likely to be looking towards the winter transfer window for solutions after a poor start to the new season. The English giants have managed just one win in seven Premier League games this season and are 13th in the league table. Last weekend, Michael Carrick’s team took the lead against Leeds United at Elland Road, but conceded late and drew the game 1-1. It was the fourth time in 11 games across competitions this season that the Red Devils have either lost or drawn a game after taking the lead. United’s inability to keep goals out has put the spotlight on the backline, which has been underperforming for a while. The defence could be a focus of INEOS’ activity in January, while they could also be tempted to sign a new left-back as Luke Shaw’s replacement. A new right-back could be on their wish list as well, with Diogo Dalot failing to impress. One player who could address both positions and also give the Red Devils an attacking edge is Wesley Franca, who has been linked with a move to Old Trafford for a while. Wesley suits United’s requirements Wesley rose through the ranks at Flamengo, before breaking into the senior side in 2021. The Brazilian was quite impressive with the South American giants, prompting AS Roma to come calling in the summer of 2025. Blessed with blistering pace, Wesley is a modern full-back who loves bombing forward and has the stamina to cover ground for the entire 90 minutes. As such, the 23-year-old hit the ground running at the Stadio Olimpico and has since become a first-team regular for the Serie A giants. This season, Wesley has registered one assist in eight appearances across competitions for Roma, all but one of which have been starts. Wesley Stats: 2026/27 Season Source: Transfermarkt . Wesley’s qualities make him a fine successor to Luke Shaw. Naturally right-footed, the Brazilian is also comfortable on the right wing, making him a possible alternative to Dalot as well. A previous report relayed by The Peoples Person suggested that United could face competition from Arsenal and Newcastle United in the race for the Roma star. It now appears that the Red Devils have stepped up their pursuit ahead of the winter transfer window. United eyeing Wesley According to Football Insider , United are contemplating a move for Wesley ahead of the January transfer window. The report states: “Manchester United are keeping tabs on Roma right-back Wesley ahead of the upcoming January transfer window, sources have told Football Insider.” The report also confirms that Arsenal and Newcastle United are in the race for the Brazilian and suggests that both clubs are ready to make a move. This season, Wesley has registered one assist in eight appearances across competitions for Roma, all but one of which have been starts. Wesley Stats: 2026/27 Season Source: Transfermarkt . Wesley’s qualities make him a fine successor to Luke Shaw. Naturally right-footed, the Brazilian is also comfortable on the right wing, making him a possible alternative to Dalot as well. A previous report relayed by The Peoples Person suggested that United could face competition from Arsenal and Newcastle United in the race for the Roma star. It now appears that the Red Devils have stepped up their pursuit ahead of the winter transfer window. United eyeing Wesley According to Football Insider , United are contemplating a move for Wesley ahead of the January transfer window. The report states: “Manchester United are keeping tabs on Roma right-back Wesley ahead of the upcoming January transfer window, sources have told Football Insider.” The report also confirms that Arsenal and Newcastle United are in the race for the Brazilian and suggests that both clubs are ready to make a move. It continues: “The Brazil international is attracting interest from several Premier League clubs at the moment, with Arsenal and Newcastle also keen to make a move.” “Sources say that Wesley’s versatility holds the ‘key’ to United’s interest, as Michael Carrick’s side are in the market for reinforcements in both full-back positions.” Roma have set a £50 million price tag on the player’s head, but that valuation could rise further. The report states that the asking price could pose a problem for United, adding: “United have been clear admirers of Wesley over a sustained period, but that price tag may prove prohibitive for them in the middle of the season.” “However, their desire to strengthen in the full-back positions remains a clear priority for the Old Trafford outfit, and Wesley has already been established as a clear target in that department.” Final Thoughts United are in serious need of reinforcements in the winter transfer window and Wesley could solve more than one problem. While prising him away from Roma will not be easy amid growing competition, the Brazilian could be a game changer for the Red Devils. Why? ✅ Wesley has previously been linked with United. ⚠️ Roma would be reluctant to part with a key player midway through the season. TPP view We believe Wesley could be on United’s wish list ahead of January, but it is too early to speculate whether INEOS will make a move for him during the winter transfer window.

item.title: England unchanged to face France after Tonga defeat
item.description: AJ Brimson, who keeps his place at full-back, scored one of England's two tries against Tonga [Getty Images] England coach Brian McDermott has named an unchanged 19-man squad for Saturday's Rugby League World Cup match against France. This is despite a 30-12 defeat by Tonga in their opening game which has put England's chances of progression to the semi-finals in danger. AJ Brimson retains his place at full-back in the XIII with Jack Welsby among the interchanges. McDermott has kept faith in his players as they prepare for Saturday's Group B-C match in Perth (kick-off 07.35 BST). England men: AJ Brimson, Dom Young, Hugo Savala, Herbie Farnworth, Zach Eckersley, George Williams, Harry Smith, Max King, Brad O'Neill, Luke Thompson, Junior Nsemba, Kai Pearce-Paul, Victor Radley. Interchange: Jez Litten, Ben Currie, Ethan Havard, Sam Walters, Jack Welsby, Matty Ashton. Reserves: Kallum Watkins, Mikey Lewis, Ben Talty. Luke Thompson will continue at prop with Morgan Knowles still not fit to play after picking up an injury before the Tonga game. And Mikey Lewis, who was a much-debated pick for the squad as one of the half-backs ahead of 2025 Super League Man Of Steel Jake Connor, remains out of the team. Harry Smith will continue alongside England captain George Williams in the half-back roles, despite both being overpowered by Tonga last weekend. That defeat, England's first ever against Tonga, has left McDermott's side with a tough task to reach the semi-finals. England must win their next two games, against France next Saturday and Papua New Guinea on 30 October, to stand a realistic chance of progression - and because of the World Cup's format, probably need to win them both by a big score. Even then, there is the strong possibility that England will not know their fate for certain until two days later, when Tonga face 2022 finalists Samoa in their last group game. Foubister, 19, to start against Australia Jenna Foubister had a superb campaign with Wigan Warriors last season [Getty Images] In contrast to McDermott, England women's coach Stuart Barrow has made a big selection change before their blockbuster meeting with co-hosts Australia on Saturday. Jenna Foubister will start at half-back, replacing Georgia Roche, after a superb year in the Super League where she was named Woman of Steel. The 19-year-old, who scored on her debut in a 62-0 win against Wales in August 2025, will partner Izzy Rowe in the halves. Rowe scored two tries and kicked nine conversions for 26 points as England opened their World Cup campaign with a 70-6 win against Wales last Saturday. She equalled the record for the most points by an individual England player in a Women's World Cup match. There are two other changes to the XIII, as Molly Jones replaces Georgia Wilson in the centres while Liv Wood plays at prop ahead of Mary Coleman. Lucie Sams is named among the interchanges as England take on reigning champions Australia in Perth with kick-off at 10.05 BST - immediately aft

Wales women: Leanne Burnell, Zoe Heeley, Jade Mullen, Hannah Bluck, Sian Williams, Amberley Ruck, Tayla Preston, Agnes Wood, Jasmine Gibbons, Emily Hughes, Georgia Cussons, Paige Travis, Bethan Dainton. Interchange: Carys Marsh, Kathryn Salter, Erin Williams, Gracie Hobbs. Reserves: Ffion Lewis, Lucia Davies, Frances Layton, Katie Carr. Tedesco replaces Walsh for Australia Reece Walsh was the star of Australia's Ashes whitewash of England last year [Getty Images] Australia coach Kevin Walters has dropped Reece Walsh to the bench for their second group game against Fiji on Sunday (09.05 GMT). James Tedesco replaces Walsh, and will captain the co-hosts and men's World Cup favourites. Walsh, who had not played since 15 August amid injury troubles, was rusty as Australia were pushed by New Zealand in a thrilling World Cup opening match last Thursday. He scored a try but kicked just two of five conversions as the Aussies squeezed to a 24-22 win at Sydney Football Stadium. Tedesco won the Clive Churchill medal for best player in the NRL Grand Final as Sydney Roosters beat Newcastle Knights 19-18 on 4 October. And he earns his place in the XIII here as one of five changes made by Walters. Bradman Best, Sam Walker and Blayke Brailey all come in for their Test debuts. Tedesco takes the captain's armband from Isaah Yeo, who is rested. Yeo has delayed surgery on a torn pectoral muscle to play at the World Cup.

item.title: “Family, I think that’s the foundation of everything,” Jota
item.description: “Family, I think that’s the foundation of everything,” Jota Jota credits his family for their massive support and contribution to helping him through the difficult 18 months on the sidelines as he worked hard to get himself fit… Jota of Celtic reacts at full time. Celtic v Hearts, Scottish Premiership, Celtic Park, 18 October 2026. Photo Mark Runnacles IMAGO Shutterstock Now the Celtic winger has returned fully prepared to resume his playing career which has essentially stalled over the few years since leaving Celtic for Saudi Arabia after the 2023 Scottish Cup Final win over Inverness Caley Thistle. Jota took the decision to travel back home to Lisbon for specialist treatment throughout the recovery process.Yet while the medical professionals were central to his return, Celtic’s Superstar from Portugal credits the help he received from his family as being hugely significant. Jota of Celtic and Jordi Altena of Hearts Celtic v Hearts, Scottish Premiership, Celtic Park, 18 October 2026 Photo Mark Runnacles Shutterstock “Family, I think that’s the foundation of everything,” Jota explained at his post match media conference on Sunday afternoon after Celtic’s emphatic 7-1 win over Hearts at Celtic Park. Jota came off the bench to replace Callum Osmand at the interval and certainly enjoyed his return to Paradise, as did the 60,000 Celtic fans who were delighted to see him return to the team. “And having them day by day next to me and knowing that no matter what, they will always be there – like when I go home – I think it’s the best feeling someone can have. “I had mine every day waiting for me to come home. And once I know they’re safe, I know that, OK, this is already a very good thing because in the end, everyone wants to have a healthy family and someone that you can build a life on. “I’m no different from anyone, even though I’m a footballer obviously, but that was always my preoccupation. Like, ‘Okay, I’m not in the best position at the moment because I’m injured, but that doesn’t mean I’m going to stop living my life’. Jota of Celtic, Celtic v Hearts, Scottish Premiership, F Celtic Park, 18 October 2026. Mark Runnacles IMAGO Shutterstock “There are more things in life from football. And I had to rewire again to get that.” “I think I’ve met some demons and I’ve had some good talks with them,” Jota admitted. “I think we developed a good relationship afterwards and we are all on the same table nowadays and we can laugh about everything that happened. “In the end, I think if you don’t grow from a situation like this, it’s because you didn’t learn anything.” Jota of Celtic celebrates after the Scottish Premiership match between Motherwell and Celtic at Fir Park on October 11, 2026. Jota of Celtic and Jordi Altena of Hearts Celtic v Hearts, Scottish Premiership, Celtic Park, 18 October 2026 Photo Mark Runnacles Shutterstock “Family, I think that’s the foundation of everything,” Jota explained at his post match media conference on Sunday afternoon after Celtic’s emphatic 7-1 win over Hearts at Celtic Park. Jota came off the bench to replace Callum Osmand at the interval and certainly enjoyed his return to Paradise, as did the 60,000 Celtic fans who were delighted to see him return to the team. “And having them day by day next to me and knowing that no matter what, they will always be there – like when I go home – I think it’s the best feeling someone can have. “I had mine every day waiting for me to come home. And once I know they’re safe, I know that, OK, this is already a very good thing because in the end, everyone wants to have a healthy family and someone that you can build a life on. “I’m no different from anyone, even though I’m a footballer obviously, but that was always my preoccupation. Like, ‘Okay, I’m not in the best position at the moment because I’m injured, but that doesn’t mean I’m going to stop living my life’. (Photo by Zak Mauger/Getty Images) From here on, Jota merits a period of injury free stability, so that he can get back to his best and contribute to the team as well as writing some happier stories for his own playing career, with hopefully the best still to come from Celtic’s Superstar from Portugal. Jota is sure that he can achieve that. “Definitely. Otherwise I wouldn’t be helpful for Celtic if I was happy with the things I did before. “So yeah, I’m very positive that good things will come. I’m accepting the present and how things are going and I’m trusting the process. I’m not thinking too much forward. Just every minute on the pitch? Yeah, just enjoy fully because it’s not granted that we’ll be here tomorrow or next week. “So I cannot predict too much stuff. item.title: Lakers face brutal $4.2M hit after Dalton Knecht mistake made one year ago comes to light
item.description: Lakers face brutal $4.2M hit after Dalton Knecht mistake made one year ago comes to light originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Lakers are very close to beginning the regular season, as they open their campaign Wednesday against the Golden State Warriors . LA is ready to start a new era, as LeBron James and several others are no longer part of the team. The Lakers had to let go of one player before Monday. The presumed option was Dalton Knecht. “My assumption is that if they had to make a decision right now, they would not pick up the $6.4 million team-option on Dalton Knecht. He's got between now and Halloween to change their mind," Lakers analyst Trevor Lane said. LA has turned away from Knecht over the last couple of years. The team simply doesn't see the same value in him as it once did. Head coach JJ Redick feels that Knecht was given enough opportunities. “I think the biggest thing is the team changed. The team changed. Needs changed, the fit changed. I think he’s gotten better as a player the last two years. I think, particularly last year, each guy got plenty of opportunities with the injuries we had. I just think coming into this year, we added a lot of wings and he’s in a tough spot right now,” Redick said. Unsurprisingly, the former first-round pick was waived on Monday. However, the Lakers made a mistake last October by picking up his contract option, meaning they will have to pay him this season. “The Lakers decided to pick up Dalton Knecht’s $4.2 million team option for 2026-27 last October, assuming at the very least they would be able to trade him. After trying for a year, they obviously found no takers and now will keep his dead money on their books for the upcoming season if he is not claimed on waivers (he won’t be). Poor asset management has become a theme for this front office over the years,” Lakers Nation’s Daniel Starkand wrote. For Knecht, this is huge, as he will still receive his money for what would have been the final year of his deal. For the Lakers, this is a situation they would have loved to avoid, as they are now stuck with the financial consequences of that decision. LA missed on this first-round pick, even though Knecht was once a highlight during his rookie season. The Lakers can now focus on the season, but their decision last October comes with a cost after Monday's move. item.title: NFL Network analyst apologises to Jalen Hurts after controversial comments over missing 2026 season
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images NFL Network’s Michael Robinson had to issue an apology statement towards Jalen Hurts and the Philadelphia Eagles after reckless comments on-air. Hurts will miss the rest of the 2026 NFL season with issues that started as a superficial blood clot in his legs to serious clots in his lungs, forcing him to miss the season to ensure a healthy recovery in time for the 2027 NFL season. With the circumstances around Hurts’ injury being up for debate, as he played through the superficial diagnosis in London on very little rest due to a 36-hour monitoring window, Robinson’s reckless comments on NFL Network drew a lot of attention. NFL Network analyst apologises to Jalen Hurts and the Eagles Robinson issued an apology on social media, regretting his decision to jokingly speculate over the nature of Hurts’ injury and absence, implying that Hurts forcefully had himself ruled out for the season because of the Eagles’ 2-4 record. “I want to sincerely apologise to Jalen Hurts, his family, the Philadelphia Eagles organisation and fan base for my comments last Thursday. They were unfounded, and I never should have speculated on a health issue of a player, nor his commitment to his team.” This is the second time in a month that an NFL analyst has tried attacking an Eagles player for their absences because of the team’s record. Stephen A. Smith minimised Lane Johnson’s mental health struggles when he retired a few weeks ago, and now Johnson did the same with Hurts’ life-threatening diagnosis. The sincerity behind the apology is being questioned by fans and experts, including Terrell Owens, who demanded via Instagram comments that Robinson apologise live on-air, in the same way he attacked Hurts. What did Michael Robinson say about Jalen Hurts? Robinson openly theorised on the NFL Network that Hurts pulled himself from availability because of the injury crisis the Eagles are going through, while also saying that this was an attempt to stop the Eagles from scapegoating him as the reason for a losing season. “if I’m Jalen Hurts − or anybody in Jalen Hurts’ camp − I’m saying, ‘Well, if everybody’s hurt, I’m hurt, too…’ To me, it looked like Jalen is kind of getting himself out of the fray so that this lost season… He’s pulling himself out so that this doesn’t look like it’s on me.” The implication from either side of the coin is terrible. Implying that a Super Bowl Champion QB would fake the severity of a life-threatening issue just to sit out the remainder of the season when he has previously played through multiple injuries to deliver winning football to Philadelphia is disrespectful. In addition, implying that the Eagles wanted to endanger Hurts and keep him on the field to scapegoat him and trade him away was completely baseless and irresponsible. The apology has been made but the impact might be a little too much to brush off with a flat apology. Read more: ‘Substation strikes again’ – 49ers fans are upset after Mike Evans’ left g

item.title: Warriors' Jimmy Butler knows when he'll return from ACL injury, keeping his target date a secret
item.description: Warriors' Jimmy Butler knows when he'll return from ACL injury, keeping his target date a secret originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Last season was a frustrating one for the Golden State Warriors , as they battled numerous injuries that ultimately caused them to miss the NBA Playoffs. One of the biggest setbacks was Steph Curry missing a significant amount of time. Another major injury was suffered by veteran Jimmy Butler, who had to undergo knee surgery after tearing his ACL. “Butler has been slowly increasing his on-court work while traveling the globe this summer, and the most recent strength tests on his right ACL recovery have shown notable progress, according to league sources. But Butler still has extensive rehab work ahead. He is expected to be limited to individual court and strength work when training camp opens in a month, league sources said, with the 36-year-old forward needing more time to be cleared for a full contact setting. A return in January or February can be considered an optimistic target," ESPN's Anthony Slater wrote. The Warriors are expected to be without Butler for at least part of the season, although the veteran has provided a positive update on his recovery. He says his knee feels great. “Great! My knee aches a little bit, but outside of that, I feel amazing. I'm super blessed to be able to play for some amazing organizations with some Hall of Fame players and I can say, I am probably with the greatest player that I have ever played with right now in this team for the greatest organization, so 16 years in and to end up over here with the Warriors, couldn't ask for a better story," Butler said. It remains unclear exactly when Butler will return, but there is at least an estimated timeline for his recovery. The veteran and the Warriors also appear to have a target date in mind. However, Butler told ESPN that he is not going to reveal it. “I know [an exact target date]," Butler said. "We know. Y'all just find out whenever y'all find out." The good news is that the recovery appears to be progressing well enough for the Warriors to have a target date in mind. Butler is a competitor, and missing this much time could only make him more motivated to return to the court. Butler could be a huge boost for Golden State once he returns, potentially making the difference in the team's playoff hopes. The Warriors seem to have an idea of when their veteran star will be back, but for everyone else, the exact date remains a mystery. He is expected to be limited to individual court and strength work when training camp opens in a month, league sources said, with the 36-year-old forward needing more time to be cleared for a full contact setting. A return in January or February can be considered an optimistic target," ESPN's Anthony Slater wrote. The Warriors are expected to be without Butler for at least part of the season, although the veteran has provided a positive update on his recovery. He says his knee feels great. “Great! My knee aches a little bit, but outside of that, I feel amazing. I'm super blessed to be able to play for some amazing organizations with some Hall of Fame players and I can say, I am probably with the greatest player that I have ever played with right now in this team for the greatest organization, so 16 years in and to end up over here with the Warriors, couldn't ask for a better story," Butler said. It remains unclear exactly when Butler will return, but there is at least an estimated timeline for his recovery. The veteran and the Warriors also appear to have a target date in mind. However, Butler told ESPN that he is not going to reveal it. “I know [an exact target date]," Butler said. "We know. Y'all just find out whenever y'all find out." The good news is that the recovery appears to be progressing well enough for the Warriors to have a target date in mind. Butler is a competitor, and missing this much time could only make him more motivated to return to the court. Butler could be a huge boost for Golden State once he returns, potentially making the difference in the team's playoff hopes. The Warriors seem to have an idea of when their veteran star will be back, but for everyone else, the exact date remains a mystery. item.title: The Hoddle of Coffee: Tottenham Hotspur News and Links for Tuesday, October 20
item.description: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 19: Dejan Kulusevski and James Maddison of Tottenham Hotspur embrace following the Premier League 2026/27 match between Tottenham Hotspur and Coventry City at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 19, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Harry Murphy - Danehouse/Getty Images) | Getty Images good morning everyone – WHAT A DAY !!!!! Tottenham Hotspur won a football match, AT HOME!!! There’s so much to be excited about here. There were moments where Spurs looked nervous, yes, but moments of brilliance. Do Spurs only score worldies? James Maddison and Omar Marmoush might say so. Oh, and then a casual trivela from Ben Davies? Get outta here baby: Ben Davies securing the three points 🙌 pic.twitter.com/Nt0WyIut40 — Tottenham Hotspur (@SpursOfficial) October 19, 2026 But I think nothing was more significant than the return of Dejan Kulusevski. He was out injured for more than 500 days. I thought his career was over. It hurt me to see. Thank goodness I was wrong. And I’m equally thankful for his doctors, physios and the team at Spurs HQ, and for Deki himself. When Roberto De Zerbi announced Kulusevski would be on the bench, I thought it was just for the vibes. And then, with Tottenham improbably ahead against Coventry on Monday, Kulusevski made an appearance on the pitch. Here’s what De Zerbi had to say, via Alasdair Gold (full transcript linked below): “Just for the fans because they waited (for) him on the pitch and in the last 5-10 minutes for extra time, we needed the support of the fans. And they are fantastic with Kulusevski, with us, they suffered too much in the last 3-4 seasons, I don’t know, but they deserve to celebrate many, many wins.“ There are a couple things I’d like to point out: Yes, we have suffered for a long time. We deserved to see Kulusevski. More importantly, he deserved to hear the crowd’s appreciation for him. He looked pretty dang good! That run he made late in the second half? My goodness, your hoddler-in-chief was jumping up and down waiting for that classic Deki cut-in just outside the box. We were close. Maybe next time. I agree with RDZ when he said there were better performances this season. But we all know wins are the most important statistic. This was a big one, and I’m going to celebrate it. Maddison was incredible, Marmoush was really good. I really liked seeing Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes. I’m still unconvinced with Jan Paul van Hecke. But we have Kulusevski back. UP THE SPURS! Fitzie’s track of the day: Fernando, by ABBA And now for your links: The Athletic ($$) : “Tottenham finally end their wait for a league win. Did Maddison just kickstart their season?” Alasdair Gold : “Every word De Zerbi said on Maddison, Kulusevski and surprising answer on new Tottenham injuries” Matt Law : “Maddison and Kulusevski bring back the feel-good factor to Spurs” BBC : “Maddison’s magic moment for Spurs – 18 months in the making” Sky Sports : “Tottenham 3-1 Coventry: Dejan Kulusevski returns to action a
