item.title: ESPN’s efforts to change Jason Kelce look to have failed after ‘epic’ Monday Night Football moment
item.description: Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Jason Kelce has given ESPN another reminder that retirement has not made him a neutral NFL observer, and his latest celebration suggests the network faces a bigger challenge than simply separating him from the Philadelphia Eagles. The former All-Pro centre has already faced questions over his habit of referring to Philadelphia as “we”, but he has now extended that loyalty to his hometown Cleveland Browns following their victory over the Baltimore Ravens. The Browns’ 4-2 start and position at the top of the AFC North gave Kelce plenty to celebrate. His reaction also renewed the debate over whether a former player should leave his personal allegiances behind when working as a television analyst. Kelce made no attempt to hide his excitement during ESPN’s coverage, celebrating Cleveland’s early success and their victory over a divisional rival. “I’m from Cleveland. We’ve been waiting for this moment, fellas. We’re finally here,” Kelce declared. He continued celebrating the Browns’ 4-2 record, repeatedly referring to the franchise as “we” while highlighting the significance of defeating Baltimore. Kelce grew up in the Cleveland area before playing college football at Cincinnati alongside his younger brother, Travis Kelce. Both brothers have maintained their connections to Cleveland sports, including appearances supporting the Cavaliers. ESPN Has Already Tried to Change Kelce’s Language Kelce’s tendency to speak like a supporter rather than a detached analyst has already created awkward moments during ESPN broadcasts. After spending 13 seasons with Philadelphia and winning a Super Bowl, the retired offensive lineman has struggled to distance himself from the franchise that defined his NFL career. His repeated use of “we” when discussing the Eagles previously prompted Pat McAfee to joke about his allegiance following Philadelphia’s defeat to the Chicago Bears. Kelce eventually apologised to Bears supporters, although former ESPN analyst Ryan Clark defended his position. ESPN producer Jeff Dufine has also acknowledged the ongoing problem. “We’ve tried to get the ‘we’ out of him,” Dufine told the Philadelphia Inquirer. The latest Cleveland celebration suggests those efforts have achieved little. Kelce’s next ESPN gig will be in Paris during Week 7’s international matchup between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France. item.title: Reese scores 30 points as Atlanta win at Golden State to level WNBA Finals
item.description: Angel Reese delivered 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals after she struggled down the stretch in the series opener, as the Atlanta Dream stymied the Golden State Valkyries at both ends in the second half to win 79-65 and level the best-of-seven series at 1-1.

item.title: Barcelona XI v PSG: Jules Koundé and Eric Garcia out, Raphinha returns
item.description: Barcelona XI v PSG: Jules Koundé and Eric Garcia out, Raphinha returns FC Barcelona pay a visit to back-to-back UEFA Champions League winners PSG for Matchday 3 of Europe’s premier club competition . Hansi Flick’s Blaugranes have won all their 11 games in all competitions this season. They also average close to four goals scored per game with Lamine Yamal hitting peak form. The 19-year-old sensation will be eager to make his mark at Paris’ Parc des Princes after tormenting France in those last two years with the Spanish national team. Flick will deploy Yamal on his favourite right-winger position as Brazilian centre-forward Raphinha returns from injury. England’s Anthony Gordon is poised to play on the left-wing. Flick is spoilt for chances up front with Dani Olmo, Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus poised to start on the bench. The same can’t be said regarding the defense. Indeed, both of Barcelona’s senior right-backs – Jules Koundé and Eric Garcia – have pulled out of the squad. L’Equipe predicts that 19-year-old Xavi Espart will be tasked with dealing with one of the best left-wingers in the world in PSG’s Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. Barcelona likely line-up v PSG Javi Garcia; João Cancelo, Gerard Martin, Pau Cubarsi, Xavi Espart; Rodri, Fermin Lopez, Pedri; Anthony Gordon, Raphinha, Lamine Yamal. (L’Éq) GFFN | Bastien Cheval

item.title: ‘Who Calls a Game Better Than Troy Aikman?’ — ESPN Legend Comes to MNF Icon’s Defense Amid Contract Drama
item.description: ‘You Know Who Calls a Game Better Than Troy Aikman?’ — Mike Wilbon Goes to Bat for ESPN Analyst Amid Contract Uncertainty Mike Wilbon, the ESPN legend who co-hosts “Pardon the Interruption,” went to bat for the network’s Monday Night Football stalwart Troy Aikman as the Dallas Cowboys legend’s contract drama continues to unravel. Aikman’s future at ESPN remains unsettled: he’s in the final year of his deal and unsigned, while his longtime booth partner, Joe Buck, has already re-signed. Front Office Sports reported last week that the two argued over their contract situations before last week’s broadcast. ESPN’s Mike Wilbon Comes Out in Troy Aikman’s Support FOS’s Ryan Glasspiegel had reported that the argument happened in the booth before the Buffalo Bills’ 37-34 overtime win over the Los Angeles Rams on October 12. The game was at SoFi Stadium, where ESPN will call its first Super Bowl in February 2027. A source told the outlet that Buck was the one who finally brought up the unspoken tension over their different contracts, and that the argument subsided before kickoff, with nothing on the broadcast to indicate anything was wrong. Wilbon opened with a question on the show he co-hosts with Tony Kornheiser that he was more than ready to answer on Monday: “You know who calls a game better than Troy Aikman?” “You knuckleheads, NOBODY calls a game better than Troy Aikman,” he said in a resounding tone. The Aikman-Buck pair landed at ESPN in the 2022 offseason, when the network signed both away from Fox on five-year deals. Aikman agreed first, and Buck followed weeks later, after Fox let him out of the final year of his contract. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Buck’s new six-year deal, which The Athletic reported in September is worth more than $100 million, runs through ESPN’s second Super Bowl in 2031, and the friction between the partners dates to that report. Aikman, whose contract is up after this season, still hasn’t received a formal offer. Days after Buck’s extension surfaced, Aikman told Richard Deitsch in a podcast that he “thought something would be done prior to the start of this season. I’ve never gone into the last year of a contract ever since I signed with the Dallas Cowboys.” Aikman also responded to the FOS report on October 15 on “96.7 The Ticket” in Dallas. “I don’t know if now is the time,” Aikman said, before turning to what comes next: “I’ll broadcast through this season, and I’ll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens. But I’m looking forward to whatever the rest of this season does hold and the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot might be.” Not everyone feels sorry for him. Bill Simmons, who left ESPN in 2015, offered another theory on “The Bill Simmons Podcast”: “But how do we know Aikman didn’t ask ESPN for like $25M, $30 million? … I don’t wanna hear the victim thing for Troy Aikman. He’s got a pretty good life.” PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL

Amazon, meanwhile, has an out in Kirk Herbstreit’s new “Thursday Night Football” deal. On ESPN’s side, Greg Olsen, who is playing out the final year of his Fox contract, is a possible successor to Aikman, while other names such as the Kelce brothers and Pat McAfee continue to be floated. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Jets’ Aaron Glenn Firmly Put on Notice Days Before Dolphins Game
item.description: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - DECEMBER 07: Head coach Mike McDaniel of the Miami Dolphins hugs head coach Aaron Glenn of the New York Jets after the game at MetLife Stadium on December 07, 2025 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) Getty Garrett Wilson labeled the Week 6 game against the New England Patriots as a “Big [Expletive] Game.” It certainly feels that way in Week 7 for New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn ahead of the Miami Dolphins game. “Sunday is a must-win for the Jets. I mean, you gotta beat the Dolphins. Now look, the Dolphins are not going to go winless. I mean, they’re not. They are going to win a couple of games, and so the Jets better be on it; otherwise, they could end up being that team. If they lost to the Dolphins, boy, woo, the Glenn watch would be on, the Glenn watch would be on because you can’t lose to the Dolphins, but we’ve seen stranger things happen,” ESPN’s Rich Cimini said on the “Jets Collective” podcast. When Cimini said we’d be on “Glenn watch,” he is referencing a potential in-season firing. Miami has been accused by fans and some media analysts of purposefully tanking to try to improve their position in the 2027 NFL Draft. If you were to lose to the team that appears to be actively trying to lose, that would be a major indictment of Glenn. Woody Johnson has owned the Jets for 26 years. He has only fired a coach midseason once during his ownership reign (Robert Saleh in 2024). For what it’s worth, that abrupt move didn’t work out for the Jets. A Fork in the Road for Glenn In Week 6, the Jets suffered another competitive loss. When those first started happening, the Jets’ baker was serving out warm moral cookies. However, that taste has quickly turned bitter because, for Glenn, it’s about winning games. The Jets sit at 2-4, suboptimal, but the next two games for the Jets are at home against winnable opponents. In Week 7, they host the winless Dolphins (0-5). In Week 8, they host the Las Vegas Raiders , who have lost three games in a row (3-3). According to Vegas Insider , the Jets are a favorite in both games: Versus Dolphins (-5.5) Versus Raiders (-1.5) If the Jets beat the opponents they’re supposed to beat, they can return to .500 on the season (4-4). That would allow the Jets to reset and get ready for the second half of the season. However, if they slip up, the Jets could dig themselves in a hole that they aren’t capable of getting out of. Lose-Lose Scenario This doesn’t feel good. If the Jets beat the Dolphins and secure Glenn’s first win in the AFC East, for a lot of fans it will ring hollow. Miami stinks, and they’re trying to tank, according to some fans and analysts. If they lose, Cimini said we could be on Glenn watch for a potential firing. Jets fans would lose their minds if they lost to what many perceive to be an inferior team. This is the ultimate lose-lose scenario. If the Jets win, they don’t get credit. If the Jets lose, hellfire will be raining from the hig

item.title: Exactly 30 years (30 years!!!) ago today Newcastle United 5 Manchester United 0 and watch here
item.description: Newcastle United v Manchester United It was 20 October 1996 at St James Park, Newcastle United 5 Manchester United 0. Yes, exactly 30 years (30 years!!!) ago to the day when we watched Kevin Keegan’s team totally dismantle the reigning champions. There was no fluke about it either, brilliant attacking play and goals that Man Utd simply had no answer to. The only negative though was that this result was seven months too late… On 4 March 1996, Newcastle had also battered Man Utd , but couldn’t put the goals on the end of it. Peter Schmeichel producing a one man show and his goal leading a charmed life, as chance after chance was created, but Newcastle just couldn’t get the goal that would surely have ensured the Premier League title that season. Instead Eric Cantona scored with pretty much the only chance the visitors had that night. Returning to 20 October 1996 and that five goal victory, this is the team that lined up: Pavel Srnicek Steve Watson Philippe Albert Darren Peacock John Beresford Robert Lee Peter Beardsley David Batty David Ginola Alan Shearer Les Ferdinand Newcastle United 5 Manchester United 0 – what memories! But was this really 30 (THIRTY!!!) years ago? Where does the time go…? Source

Peter Schmeichel producing a one man show and his goal leading a charmed life, as chance after chance was created, but Newcastle just couldn’t get the goal that would surely have ensured the Premier League title that season. Instead Eric Cantona scored with pretty much the only chance the visitors had that night. Returning to 20 October 1996 and that five goal victory, this is the team that lined up: Pavel Srnicek Steve Watson Philippe Albert Darren Peacock John Beresford Robert Lee Peter Beardsley David Batty David Ginola Alan Shearer Les Ferdinand Newcastle United 5 Manchester United 0 – what memories! But was this really 30 (THIRTY!!!) years ago? Where does the time go…? Source

item.title: Kevin Cash’s post-ALCS comments will have Rays fans booking flights to Milwaukee
item.description: Credit: Jonathan Dyer-Imagn Images Kevin Cash’s post-ALCS comments will have Rays fans booking flights to Milwaukee appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tampa Bay Rays are headed to the World Series for the third time in franchise history after finishing off the Cleveland Guardians in Game 6 of the ALCS on Monday night, 7-3. After two disappointing seasons that saw them fall out of the postseason entirely, the Rays have shown that their strong 2026 campaign, which had them winning the AL East division title with a record of 98-64, was no mere fluke. But of course, the job is far from finished. The Rays are going to face the best team in MLB this year in the Milwaukee Brewers, the team that won 103 games in the regular season and even swept the reigning World Series champion Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS. Suffice to say, the road ahead is only about to get more difficult for the AL pennant winner. Nonetheless, manager Kevin Cash is instilling so much confidence in the Rays clubhouse that fans might have to book a flight to Milwaukee to catch Game 1 and Game 2 of the World Series live. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “We got one more bite!” Cash said as he kicked off the Rays’ locker room celebration, via B/R Walk Off on X. “I think we got a flight to Milwaukee!” Kevin Cash and the Rays are headed to the World Series 🍾 pic.twitter.com/km0RcOg5oQ — B/R Walk-Off (@BRWalkoff) October 20, 2026 It’s an incredible achievement for the Rays and Brewers to have made it this far. These two teams operate on shoestring budgets relative to the big-market teams, ranking 28th and 19th, respectively, in player payroll for this year. But there is only going to be one team left standing at the end of this season, The stakes are even higher for both teams considering that these two franchises have never won a World Series title, with the Rays suffering heartbreaking defeats in 2008 and 2020 and the Brewers falling short all the way back in 1982. Perhaps the third time’s the charm for the Rays; Cash knows the pain of losing on the grand World Series stage, as he was Tampa Bay’s manager six years ago, so perhaps the lessons he’s learned from that defeat will be enough for them to be able to get over the hump. Related: Why the Rays don’t have what it takes to beat Brewers in the World Series Related: Freddy Peralta’s wild run with Rays is like no other since 1968

item.title: 49ers WR Mike Evans’ Achilles injury gets huge update after MNF win vs. Commanders
item.description: Kyle Terada-Imagn Images 49ers WR Mike Evans’ Achilles injury gets huge update after MNF win vs. Commanders appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Francisco 49ers suffered a brutal blow in Week 6 against the Washington Commanders. Despite getting the win in prime time , San Francisco fans were restless after Mike Evans exited the game with an injury. Given the state of the current wide receiver room, losing yet another wide receiver to an injury was the last thing this team needed in their quest to win the Super Bowl. Thankfully, the 49ers got a positive update about their star wide receiver after the game. Kyle Shanahan said that the Achilles injury he suffered was already bothering him before the game. A flare-up of that injury led to his early exit against the Commanders. “Kyle doesn’t believe more testing is required, that Evans has dealt with this in his career, was touch-and-go whether he’d play after not practicing last week,” Cam Inman reported on X. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The 49ers already have nearly their entire wide receiver room out with an injury. They already lost Ricky Pearsall earlier in the year due to complications in his injured knee. Rookie De’Zhaun Stribling suffered a serious ankle injury in Week 1 that ruled him out for the season. Christian Kirk suffered an injury in training camp, while Demarcus Robinson also injured his ankle in Week 2 of the season. Does this update mean that Evans will be available for Week 7? It’s not conclusive yet, but the good news for the 49ers is that he likely won’t miss extended time. Losing Evans would mean that San Francisco will rely on Brandin Cooks, Jacob Cowing, Jordan Watkins, and a potential return from Deebo Samuel Sr. The 49ers are also set to get some reinforcements in Week 7. Shanahan also said in his post-game interview that Kirk is likely to play in Week 7 against the Atlanta Falcons. San Francisco also still has two of the best offensive weapons in the league in tight end George Kittle and running back Christian McCaffrey. Related: Of course the Pat McAfee Commanders-49ers MNF broadcast was unhinged Related: 49ers’ George Kittle sounds off on San Francisco’s approach amid scorching 6-0 start

item.title: Of course the Pat McAfee Commanders-49ers MNF broadcast was unhinged
item.description: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images Of course the Pat McAfee Commanders-49ers MNF broadcast was unhinged appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Francisco 49ers stayed unblemished on Monday, beating the Washington Commanders , 23-17, at Levi’s Stadium to improve to 6-0. The Commanders, on the other hand, fell to 1-4-1. The 49ers made key defensive stops to preserve their immaculate record after the Commanders came within striking distance in the fourth quarter. Aside from the on-field action, the game was extra entertaining for viewers because of “The Pat McAfee Show.” In the third quarter, McAfee and Dan Orlovsky got into an off-the-cuff conversation while they were kneeling on the field near the end zone. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “He’s (Orlovsky) on two knees. He’s on two knees here. Never seen anybody do this before. Obviously, taking a knee is something you do in football since high school,” said McAfee. “You ever go to a Catholic Mass? You sit and stand up, (kneel) down,” replied Orlovsky. “We’re at a football game! And you know what I’ve been doing in football is take a knee! Take a knee! Take a knee! You say, ‘You know what, how about two? Let me serve this game for you,'” added McAfee. Orlovsky doubled down and did a suggestive motion, albeit unknowingly. What are you doing @danorlovsky7 😂😂 #PMSMNFonESPN2 pic.twitter.com/4AukK1GchM — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) October 20, 2026 Fans enjoyed the candid banter. “Dan O is the best. One of one 😆😂,” said @DaveSnow72. “Dan O has such an innocent mind 😂. Talking about two knees and doing a motion. Never mind 😂. He must not realize what people think of, ah never mind. Forget it,” added @shisto5. “You get to do ‘MNF alt broadcast, but you don’t get chairs.’ Hell of a job fighting through the bean counters obstacles #getthemanachair,” wrote @DukeJohnsonPPR. “Dan is used to running out of the back of the end zone,” joked @MikeHawkNow. “McAfee funny AF,” commented @theVAUGHSAGE. The unpredictable nature of “The Pat McAfee Show” has made it hugely popular. Last year, it averaged 436,000 viewers. McAfee and ESPN are discussing a contract extension projected to pay him around $60 million per year. Related: Troy Aikman drops wild anti-analytics take during 49er-Commanders MNF tilt Related: NFL fans trash Train singer’s National Anthem attempt before MNF 49ers-Commanderes clash

item.title: Raptors predicted to trade for $186M rebounding machine to pair with Kawhi Leonard in mega deal
item.description: Raptors predicted to trade for $186M rebounding machine to pair with Kawhi Leonard in mega deal originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It is no secret that the Sacramento Kings have been looking to trade Domantas Sabonis this offseason as they try to offload his contract. The big man has been an excellent rebounder throughout his career, but his time in Sacramento could eventually come to an end. Sabonis has led the league in rebounding multiple times. Over the summer, Sacramento reportedly tried to complete a trade with the Detroit Pistons involving Sabonis. “There was a trade on the table from the Kings for Jalen Duren. They were willing to offer Domantas Sabonis to the Pistons but that's not what the Pistons want. They want to bring Jalen Duren back and secure him on a long term deal," ClutchPoints' Brett Siegel stated. During the offseason, Sabonis also switched agents. The move has raised questions about whether a trade could be on the horizon. “I do think it’s somewhat interesting that he changed agents this offseason," ESPN’s Brian Windhorst said. "He hired Aaron Mintz from CAA. This last year, Mintz and his group executed the trade for Trae Young away from Atlanta. They executed the trade for Walker Kessler away from [the Jazz ]. Domantas Sabonis just hired him. At the risk of parodying myself, why would he do that?” CBS Sports’ Sam Quinn believes the Kings should consider trading Sabonis to the Toronto Raptors in exchange for Jakob Poeltl and RJ Barrett. “Toronto sniffed around at last year's deadline. The Raptors are so loaded defensively that they can cover his vulnerabilities on that end of the floor, and the Poeltl and Barrett contracts cover matching salary if the Kings are willing to take them. The Raptors traded for a former All-Star center when they won the 2019 championship. Maybe history repeats itself,” Quinn wrote. This could be a beneficial move for the Raptors, who would add another physical rebounder alongside Kawhi Leonard. Toronto appears to be going all-in after acquiring Leonard, and a deal for Sabonis could further strengthen its roster. Sabonis is currently under a $186 million contract with Sacramento. For the Kings, this proposed deal would bring back Barrett and Poeltl, giving them a different combination of perimeter scoring and interior presence. However, the Raptors are chasing a championship, and adding a player of Sabonis' caliber could help them compete in a crowded Eastern Conference. More NBA news: Lakers finally waive Dalton Knecht after failed trade talks ahead of season opener vs. Warriors Warriors get concerning injury update on player not named Steph Curry for season opener vs. Lakers 76ers sign 7-foot-6 gigantic rim finisher to potentially pair with LeBron James, Jaylen Brown Knicks' Mike Brown details why Bruce Brown was cut over James Wiseman despite fit with team

item.title: 49ers’ George Kittle sounds off on San Francisco’s approach amid scorching 6-0 start
item.description: Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images 49ers’ George Kittle sounds off on San Francisco’s approach amid scorching 6-0 start appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Kyle Shanahan’s San Francisco 49ers are 6-0 and trending toward a possible unbeaten season that would match the ’72 Dolphins after a huge win over the Washington Commanders. The Week 6 win didn’t come without trouble as Mike Evans suffered an Achilles injury that knocked him out of the game. George Kittle , a touchdown catch recipient from Brock Purdy early on in the Commanders game, sounded off on the 49ers’ hot start after the game in comments made to ESPN’s Sportscenter. “That’s our goal, right, when we talk about it, it’s like, ‘Hey, I’m in year ten right now, I just want to win,'” Kittle said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “If you look at the big picture too much, I think it adds way too much pressure…And like, that’s all it is, so I think we’re doing a really good job this year, of like, one week that’s all that matters.” Kittle added that starting fullback Kyle Juszczyk helped the team adopt its Week 6 strategy of focusing on the Commanders game and getting a win at all costs ahead of its October 25 game at the Falcons. The result was an early lead for Brock Purdy’s team as Kittle opened the game’s scoring with a brilliant 11-yard scoring catch on a route to the middle-left corner of the end zone that was picture perfect in idea and execution. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris’ unit shut the door with a sack from Romello Height on Jayden Daniels that ended up as one of the walk-off variety. The 49ers are 6-0, and Kittle believes he has the formula for more wins, with few fans doubting it ahead of Week 7. Related: 49ers WR Mike Evans’ Achilles injury gets huge update after MNF win vs. Commanders Related: Of course the Pat McAfee Commanders-49ers MNF broadcast was unhinged

item.title: Leipzig manager Martin Demichelis highlights Real Madrid’s biggest threat and praises Diomande: ‘He makes all the difference’
item.description: Leipzig manager Martin Demichelis highlights Real Madrid’s biggest threat and praises Diomande: ‘He makes all the difference’ RB Leipzig manager Martin Demichelis has challenged his team to show a different side against Real Madrid in their upcoming UEFA Champions League meeting, insisting that the 6-1 defeat to Bayern Munich does not reflect his side’s true identity. Speaking to AS , the Argentine coach discussed the challenge awaiting Leipzig, praised Real Madrid’s depth and highlighted the threat posed by their devastating attacking transitions. Demichelis made clear that Leipzig must respond with greater confidence and a commitment to their possession-based approach. While he recognises the quality available to Jose Mourinho, he believes his team can offer a far stronger performance than they produced against Bayern. Demichelis demands a strong response against Real Madrid The heavy defeat to Bayern has put Leipzig under pressure ahead of a demanding European fixture. Demichelis, however, does not want that result to define his side’s performance at the Bernabeu. Demichelis knows the kind of threat Real Madrid possess. (Photo by Fabio Deinert/Getty Images) He expects his players to retain possession more effectively and show greater courage against a team that punishes mistakes quickly. “As a manager, I certainly hope to see a different side to the one we were last weekend, because I believe that’s exactly what we are. We’re a completely different team to the one we were. “Hopefully we’ll be much more daring, that we will actually be ourselves – a team that wants to keep possession. “Against Madrid, we have to hold onto the ball because every time they make a counter-attack, they create danger. “Take Mbappe, for example: he shows that they only need two passes for any of their forwards to break the defence, squeeze into spaces where there’s barely any room, and with a single dribble, beat the goalkeeper and, without even putting his other foot down, finish the move. That’s why he’s one of a kind. “We’ll need to be very alert to Real Madrid’s lightning-fast attacking transitions whilst, at the same time, being able to get into the game ourselves. “Jose’s teams are very much characterised by that – by being compact, by knowing when to win the ball back and when to strike,” he analysed. Real Madrid’s squad depth earns Demichelis’ respect Demichelis was equally emphatic when discussing the quality of Madrid’s midfield. The club has moved on from the celebrated combination of Luka Modric, Toni Kroos and Casemiro, but the Leipzig manager believes their current options remain among the best in the game. “The only thing I can say – because we’ve been analysing Real Madrid recently – is that, regardless of who plays, whether it’s Fede Valverde, Tchouameni, Camavinga or Bellingham starting… they’re all very good; they’re all at international level. “What Real Madrid can’t do is complain about their squad. (Photo by Fabio Deinert/Getty Images) He expects his players to retain possession more effectively and show greater courage against a team that punishes mistakes quickly. “As a manager, I certainly hope to see a different side to the one we were last weekend, because I believe that’s exactly what we are. That’s why he’s one of a kind. “We’ll need to be very alert to Real Madrid’s lightning-fast attacking transitions whilst, at the same time, being able to get into the game ourselves. “Jose’s teams are very much characterised by that – by being compact, by knowing when to win the ball back and when to strike,” he analysed. Real Madrid’s squad depth earns Demichelis’ respect Demichelis was equally emphatic when discussing the quality of Madrid’s midfield. The club has moved on from the celebrated combination of Luka Modric, Toni Kroos and Casemiro, but the Leipzig manager believes their current options remain among the best in the game. “The only thing I can say – because we’ve been analysing Real Madrid recently – is that, regardless of who plays, whether it’s Fede Valverde, Tchouameni, Camavinga or Bellingham starting… they’re all very good; they’re all at international level. “What Real Madrid can’t do is complain about their squad. Regardless of who plays and the trend in recent years regarding signings – whilst it’s true that Modric, Kroos and Casemiro have marked a wonderful and, above all, highly successful era in the club’s history – the players who are there now also possess enormous ability and, above all, are already key players for their national teams.” Yan Diomande earns praise for his development Martin Demichelis has praised Yan Diomande. (Photo by Leonhard Simon/Getty Images) The interview also touched on Yan Diomande, whose breakthrough at Real Madrid has attracted attention. Demichelis acknowledged that his direct experience of the player at Leipzig was limited, explaining that Diomande spent much of that period away with the national team and trained individually after returning. “I didn’t get to enjoy it much. I’d been appointed Leipzig’s manager in July and the player was at the World Cup, so I know Yan practically more from watching him on television. “During the few days he spent with us after the World Cup, he trained on his own. I had a few conversations with him, during which he expressed his desire to take his career to the next level. “I predict a great future for him because his development here was very rapid. “Yan is one of those players who currently makes all the difference, whether on the left or the right, thanks to his superb ball control with both feet,” he concluded.

item.title: Barcelona set their sights on €65m-rated Aston Villa star but face competition from Bayern Munich
item.description: Barcelona set their sights on €65m-rated Aston Villa star but face competition from Bayern Munich Barcelona are monitoring Aston Villa midfielder Johan Manzambi as Deco assesses potential reinforcements for the summer transfer window, according to a report from MARCA . The 21-year-old Switzerland international has attracted interest from several leading European clubs following his impressive start at Villa, although a move away from the Premier League side is not expected to be simple. As per the outlet, Bayern Munich are also keeping a close eye on Manzambi, having followed his progress since his time at Freiburg. With Aston Villa having invested €60 million to secure his transfer this summer, Barcelona could face a significant financial obstacle if they decide to turn their interest into a concrete offer. Barcelona join Bayern Munich in monitoring Johan Manzambi Manzambi’s development has caught the attention of scouts across Europe, putting the young midfielder on the radar of clubs looking for high-potential additions. English journalist Graeme Bailey, quoted by MARCA, highlighted the growing excitement surrounding the Swiss international. “We know that scouts from some of Europe’s top clubs have been very impressed by Manzambi’s performances. Barcelona have Johan Manzambi on their radar. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) “Several of them regard him as a ‘superstar in the making’. Work is already underway behind the scenes, whilst potential suitors assess his development and long-term prospects,” said Bailey. For now, Barcelona and Bayern Munich are among the clubs following his situation closely. His recent attacking output has added to the interest, as Manzambi has registered three goals and three assists in six matches this season. Aston Villa price tag could complicate Barcelona move Barcelona’s interest does not necessarily mean a transfer is imminent. The club’s financial considerations remain central to its recruitment strategy, and the cost of persuading Aston Villa to part with a player they have invested heavily in could prove prohibitive. Manzambi is also viewed as a developing talent rather than an established player whose future is already settled. Johan Manzambi will not leave Aston Villa in January. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) Barcelona’s sporting management is therefore understood to be considering him as a possible summer addition, particularly if a departure from the current squad creates room for a new arrival. That conditional approach could be important, as any pursuit would depend not only on the midfielder’s development but also on Barcelona’s financial flexibility and the competition for his signature. item.title: ‘To Think He Was Mr. Irrelevant,’ ‘Where’s Josh Allen?’ — NFL Fans React as Brock Purdy Officially Tallies Highest Career Passer Rating of All Time
item.description: Oct 19, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy (13) throws a pass during the fourth quarter against the Washington Commanders at Levi's Stadium. © Kyle Terada-Imagn Images For Brock Purdy, Monday night brought another victory and a place in the NFL record books. The San Francisco 49ers QB went 21-of-29 for 264 yards and a touchdown with no interceptions in a 23-17 win over the Washington Commanders at Levi’s Stadium. Along the way, he became the highest-rated passer in NFL history. The NFL’s post crowning Purdy made the rounds, and reaction to his historic night ran from MVP talk to, somehow, a question about Josh Allen. Brock Purdy Takes Career Passer Rating Crown Notably, career passer rating rankings count only quarterbacks with at least 1,500 attempts. Purdy entered the week five attempts shy of that mark. He wasted little time getting the 49ers going, hitting Mike Evans for 24 yards on the third play of the game and capping the opening drive with an 11-yard touchdown pass to George Kittle. Christian McCaffrey also scored on two 1-yard runs as the 49ers took a 20-3 lead into the break. Even though Jayden Daniels threw two second-half touchdown passes to pull the Commanders (1-4-1) within 23-17, it was not enough. Entering the game, Purdy’s passer rating came in at 105.4, while Lamar Jackson’s mark reads 102.7, and Aaron Rodgers is at 101.8. The Niners star finished the night with a 111.9 rating, and the NFL’s social media post had his career mark at 105.6 by the end of it. Former Green Bay Packers QB Kurt Benkert pointed to the work behind the milestone: “I was Brock’s immediate backup for 3 months during his rookie season and ran routes for him after practice every day while he went through the plays he didn’t get reps of. His preparation was second to none well before he became who he is now.” One fan seized on Purdy’s draft-day detail: “Love this, and to think he was Mr. Irrelevant!” Another fan took the long view: “Watching one of the all-time greats in the making. Even if you hate the 49ers, enjoy it. Appreciate this kid’s journey.” A third fan went straight to the most-important conversation: “MVP.” However, not every reaction was a celebration. This fan had one question: “Where’s Josh Allen?” Earlier, 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak, speaking after practice Friday, Oct. 16, three days before the milestone, had a different take on passer rating: “I don’t look at it. It’s a reflection of your unit and how you guys are playing together. So that’s not to take away from Brock. Brock’s been awesome for five years, but I would think he’d say the same thing.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Purdy also addressed it similarly: “I’m not getting done with games going, ‘Alright, was my rating at least 100 and something?’ I could really care less about that. I guess that maybe reflects, though, playing pretty good quarterback play, so I’m not trying to act like it’s nothing.”

Pro Football Network’s NFL QB Impact Grade has him at 90.8 for the season through Week 6, the top-ranked quarterback of 34 graded. Monday’s win moved the 49ers to 6-0 and first in the NFC West, their best start since they won their first eight games in 2019 on the way to a Super Bowl appearance. They visit the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7 on Sunday, Oct. 25, at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Graeme Souness calls Bukayo Saka a ‘cheat’ and claims Arsenal star ‘dives all over the place’
item.description: Graeme Souness calls Bukayo Saka a ‘cheat’ and claims Arsenal star ‘dives all over the place’ Graeme Souness has branded Arsenal forward Bukayo Saka a cheat, accusing him of diving to win free-kicks. The former Liverpool captain made the explosive comments during an appearance on Piers Morgan’s Football Uncensored . He argued that Saka goes to ground too easily and that Arsenal players put pressure on referees to influence their decisions. Souness insisted the England international, almost always among the Premier League’s most-fouled players, should stay on his feet rather than exaggerate contact. “Your man Saka dives all over the place. I don’t want to hear about him. The minute he looks like losing possession, he’s down,” Souness said to Morgan, an Arsenal fan. He added: “He simulates a foul. Anyone who simulates a foul in my book would be a cheat.” The 71-year-old also accused Arsenal players of surrounding referees whenever Saka goes down, claiming their reactions can force officials to reconsider their initial judgement. According to Souness, the winger’s screams and his teammates’ protests can persuade referees to award fouls they would otherwise ignore. He acknowledged that simulation is a widespread problem in modern football. However, Morgan strongly disagreed with Souness on the Saka accusation. Many might remember the controversial incident involving Saka and Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer during their Champions League quarter-final meeting in April 2024. Saka went down after appearing to make contact with Neuer inside the penalty area, but Arsenal were denied a late spot-kick. Replays suggested the winger moved his leg towards the goalkeeper, prompting criticism from several pundits. Attacking players with an X-factor like Saka are routinely targeted during matches as opponents look for ways to limit their impact. Branding him a cheat is a bit over the top, even for a man renowned for exaggerated comments like Souness. For a pundit who should know better, throwing around the word ‘cheat’ so casually says more about his own judgment than it does about Saka.

item.title: 49ers, Jaguars Floated Trade Idea Involving $14.6 Million Player
item.description: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) Getty The San Francisco 49ers appear to be one of the buyers ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. So far this 2026 NFL season, the Niners have established themselves as a Super Bowl contender. Despite the impressive start to the campaign, San Francisco does have areas of concern such as the wide receiver position. During the game against the Washington Commanders, the Niners saw Mike Evans leave the game due to an Achilles injury . Moreover, the Niners are dealing with injuries to other wide receivers, so the question is whether San Francisco will pursue a wideout around the trade deadline. In an Oct. 18 article , Zachary Rotman of FanSided listed the 49ers as a realistic landing spot for Jacksonville Jaguars’ Brian Thomas Jr. As part of his trade idea, Rotman has the 49ers giving a 2027 second-round pick for the former first-round pick, who is still on his rookie contract worth $14.6 million . “No team needs Thomas more than the San Francisco 49ers, who are without Ricky Pearsall for the year, De’Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson for a while, and Brandon Aiyuk for who knows how long?” Rotman wrote in his article. “Not to mention Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel have been banged up and are on the wrong side of 30. They need a receiver in the worst way.” 49ers Shouldn’t Hesitate to Give Up Day 2 Pick Moreover, while giving up a Day 2 pick is a major decision, Rotman believes that because the 49ers are in a Super Bowl window, they need to take advantage of it. “They’re legitimate Super Bowl contenders, and their odds of hoisting the Lombardi Trophy would only rise with Thomas in the fold,” Rotman added in his article. “A second-rounder is not nothing, but the Niners are a win-now team and need to act like it. “As for Jacksonville, if they need to trade Thomas, sending him to the NFC, where he’d only be an issue in the Super Bowl, makes the most sense. They’d still get a second-round pick, which is valuable, in exchange for a player whose role in their offense is hard to spot. Seems like a pretty good deal for both sides. Could the Niners Reunite With DeForest Buckner? Another potential name in the trade speculation conversation is Indianapolis Colts ‘ DeForest Buckner. Moreover, Buckner expressed his frustration after the Colts’ loss to the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 18. “I’m sick and tired of the same song and dance every year,” Buckner told reporters . These comments and the trade deadline nearing are causing conversation about whether the veteran can be a serious trade target for the team he played for from 2016 to 2019. item.title: Steelers’ Patrick Graham suddenly brings up retirement after question about Paris game
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Steelers’ Patrick Graham suddenly brings up retirement after question about Paris game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Pittsburgh Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham is already envisioning his life after football, but fans can take a deep breath; he is not stepping away anytime soon. Ahead of the team’s upcoming international showdown in Paris, France, the veteran coach brought up his post-coaching retirement plans with a laugh. Having already coached in three NFL international series games across London, twice at Wembley Stadium and once at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Graham expressed genuine excitement about adding Paris to his personal travel list. “I’ve told you, that’s where I’m going when I retire, I’m out of here,” Graham joked to reporters. “Somewhere in Europe, so, to be able to be a part of it, I’ve been a part of three games, you know. Wembley twice, in Tottenham one time, and to be in Paris to play a game, this is going to be pretty cool.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) TRENDING: Pittsburgh #Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham says he plans on moving to Europe when he retires, despite the recent reports of riots and looting in Paris. “That’s where I’m going when I retire. I’m out of here. Somewhere in Europe.” pic.twitter.com/BfsyJV2Uh1 — MLFootball (@MLFootball) October 20, 2026 Before packing any bags for France, Graham’s unit had to orchestrate a dramatic second-half turnaround. The Pittsburgh Steelers rallied from a 13-point fourth-quarter deficit to pull off a thrilling 26-19 overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Graham brought relentless heat in the fourth quarter and overtime, dialing up clever simulated pressures to throw Tampa Bay off rhythm. Cornerback Jalen Ramsey spearheaded the effort with a dominant stat line, racking up 10 tackles, four tackles for loss, and two sacks, including the game-ending sack in extra time. Outside linebacker Nick Herbig chipped in with two sacks of his own as Pittsburgh shut down the Buccaneers when it mattered most. On the other side of the ball, rookie wide receiver Germie Bernard made history with a team rookie record 11 catches for 87 yards and a touchdown, while kicker Chris Boswell provided four clutch field goals. Riding high off their first 13-plus point fourth-quarter comeback since 1992, Graham and the Steelers are taking their momentum overseas. If his defense keeps delivering game-winning plays like Sunday’s, Graham might end up putting those European retirement dreams on hold just a bit longer. Related: Steelers sign Aaron Rodgers favorite to the practice squad Related: Aaron Rodgers’ family finally makes it to Steelers game after reconciliation

item.title: The Steph Curry scare that reveals the NBA’s hidden problem
item.description: Steph Curry flapped his arms and ripped the gumshield from his mouth and stumbled towards the locker room. The open practice for the Warriors, 48 hours before the 2026/27 NBA season gets underway, delivered a chill throughout the arena. A deathly silence was palpable, knowing the precarious foundation of the Golden State’s hopes and dreams, pinned to No 30. LeBron James ’s seismic switch from Los Angeles to Philadelphia has somewhat obscured the curious situation of a 38-year-old legend’s final act. In the immediate aftermath of Curry’s misstep, irresponsible speculation spread of an ACL tear, which would all but scupper an 18th NBA season. But encouraging news since suggests merely a right ankle injury. Curry maintained he was “fine” to ease fears. But this injury scare underlined a growing concern not just for the Warriors, who start their season against the Lakers on Wednesday night. Beyond an inevitable rebuild in a post-Curry world, the NBA’s grand plans for global relevance are up against the might of the NFL’s dominance and ambitious competition from other sports internationally. A star-driven league, in the way the NFL is not necessarily, the NBA is experiencing a changing of the guard with an influx of international superstars after a soon-to-be nine-year gap since the last American MVP (James Harden in 2017/18). The NBA was absent from the 2025 Sportico 100, which showcases the most-watched US telecasts each year, a sixth straight year, with the American gluttony for the NFL illustrated by 84 events in the list. For those already initiated, the NBA is a compelling product and at first glance should soar in the coming years. Just look at last year’s finals and the Knicks’ first title in 53 years. The captivating nature of Jalen Brunson guiding New York past the Spurs, led by the most talented player of a generation, Victor Wembanyama, who emerged as a villain in the Big Apple, sets the table for a generation-defining rivalry. item.content:encoded: Steph Curry flapped his arms and ripped the gumshield from his mouth and stumbled towards the locker room. The open practice for the Warriors, 48 hours before the 2026/27 NBA season gets underway, delivered a chill throughout the arena. A deathly silence was palpable, knowing the precarious foundation of the Golden State’s hopes and dreams, pinned to No 30. LeBron James ’s seismic switch from Los Angeles to Philadelphia has somewhat obscured the curious situation of a 38-year-old legend’s final act. In the immediate aftermath of Curry’s misstep, irresponsible speculation spread of an ACL tear, which would all but scupper an 18th NBA season. But encouraging news since suggests merely a right ankle injury. Curry maintained he was “fine” to ease fears. But this injury scare underlined a growing concern not just for the Warriors, who start their season against the Lakers on Wednesday night. Beyond an inevitable rebuild in a post-Curry world, the NBA’s grand plans for global relevance are up against the might of the NFL’s dominance and ambitious competition from other sports internationally. A star-driven league, in the way the NFL is not necessarily, the NBA is experiencing a changing of the guard with an influx of international superstars after a soon-to-be nine-year gap since the last American MVP (James Harden in 2017/18). The NBA was absent from the 2025 Sportico 100, which showcases the most-watched US telecasts each year, a sixth straight year, with the American gluttony for the NFL illustrated by 84 events in the list. For those already initiated, the NBA is a compelling product and at first glance should soar in the coming years. Just look at last year’s finals and the Knicks’ first title in 53 years. The captivating nature of Jalen Brunson guiding New York past the Spurs, led by the most talented player of a generation, Victor Wembanyama, who emerged as a villain in the Big Apple, sets the table for a generation-defining rivalry. The precarious foundation of the Golden State’s hopes and dreams are pinned to No 30, Curry (AP) This writer witnessed how World Cup mania belatedly arrived in New York thanks to that Knicks run , underlining that the ingredients are there to muscle in on the NFL and Premier League in the relentless pursuit for content. There have been eight different champions in as many years, though the league must better harness that unpredictable nature to thrive. A ninth could emerge in Philadelphia, with LeBron James, seeking title No 5 and aiming to snap a seven-year drought, fresh from an unlikely switch from Los Angeles Lakers to 76ers. He joins Jaylen Brown, the Robin to Jayson Tatum as Batman for so long in Boston, alongside Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey to form the latest NBA super team. While two-time reigning MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the uber efficient Oklahoma City Thunder, champions in 2025, are the favourites once again. Commissioner Adam Silver has genuine authority and ideas, with the NBA Cup adding a wrinkle to major league tradition in the United States. But even with the exciting plans to launch NBA Europe and tie franchises to the continent’s leading football clubs, something is missing. LeBron James, Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey of the Philadelphia 76ers look on (Getty) Speaking about his plans to utilise Curry, though Philadelphia’s Nick Nurse may encounter similar issues with James and the injury-prone Embiid, Golden State head coach Steve Kerr spoke of the awkward dilemma surrounding Curry’s usage, perhaps highlighting how the next generation of superstar American basketball players are yet to take the throne of Curry, James and more. Curry remains one of the most compelling athletes in sport, with thousands flocking to catch a glimpse of him during his final years playing. You could feel the allure even outside of NBA circles during the 2024 Olympics two years ago, when Curry elevated his game and captivated a global audience en route to gold. I can even recall the swoosh of the net reverberating around the Bercy Arena, Paris as fans held their breath during Curry’s iconic warm-up routine. “We’ll start trying to map out, week by week, what’s what,” Kerr said of Curry’s usage before that injury scare, with the widely-accepted greatest shooter of all time dealing with a nagging right knee injury that cost him 39 games last term. “But to be really frank, every year we run into this [situation] where, if we have a bunch of games stacked together, back-to-backs, we have fans that buy tickets expecting to see Steph – usually Steph, sometimes other players, people expecting to see vets – and then we have a back-to-back, and we don’t play ’em. So, I would just come out and tell the fans out there to be mindful when you’re buying the tickets of the schedule. Take a look. Because we’ve got not just Steph but multiple vets we are going to try and manage, because it’s the only way we can do this.” Golden State are not alone, but with 15 back-to-backs, the value of those Warriors games are drastically reduced both at the game and on televisions around the world, a growing issue as Silver bids to retain audiences in the regular season before the exhilarating playoffs begin on 13 April with the play-in tournament. Steph Curry is a major doubt for the opening game of the season but appears to have avoided a season-ending injury (AP) Until then, the numerous shooting stars in this sport’s galaxy include the NBA Cup, a Christmas Day feast of five back-to-back games, international games aplenty, including Spurs v Pelicans in Manchester, a trade frenzy building to the 11 February deadline and the ever-evolving All-Star game. Sometimes less is more and protecting Curry, James and the league’s best veteran superstars remains paramount to the league’s ultimate success. The 2026/27 NBA season returns to Sky Sports and NOW from 20 October

item.title: Weekday CUSA Previews: 2026 Week 8
item.description: Sep 26, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; Missouri State Bears quarterback Henry Belin IV (2) throws the ball during the second half against the SMU Mustangsat Gerald J. Ford Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cherish these Tuesday and Wednesday nights. We have two weeks of Weekday CUSA remaining before the conference hands the baton to Midweek MACtion in November. Last week, Weekday CUSA delivered with several thrillers. Three of the four games featured a go-ahead score in the final 3:30 of action, and these three were all decided by exactly three points. There are two double-digit spreads this week, but we’ve seen stranger things happen on Weekday CUSA in the past. Miami, Newark, Huntsville, and Kennesaw serve as the hosts as the four-game slate spans three nights this week. Middle Tennessee-FIU and Missouri State-Delaware are set for Tuesday. New Mexico State-Sam Houston is a standalone Wednesday night game. And Liberty-Kennesaw State concludes Week 8 of CUSA play on Thursday. Here is a preview of all four matchups: Middle Tennessee @ FIU Tuesday, Oct. 20 at 7 pm ET on CBS Sports Network Spread: FIU (-10) Over/under: 45.5 Middle Tennessee (3-3, 1-1 CUSA) has its best team in the three years of the Derek Mason era. The Blue Raiders have already matched their highest win total under Mason, and there are six games left on the regular season schedule. One reason for the Blue Raiders’ rapid ascension is the play of Roman Gagliano. The sophomore quarterback threw for 291 yards and three touchdowns last week to lead a back-and-forth win over Delaware. Gagliano has been complemented well by his receivers, including Cam’ron Lacy (369 yards, 4 TD), Markus Allen (176 yards, 1 TD), and Neo Clifton (166 yards, 3 TD). Middle Tennessee’s greatest weakness earlier in the season was its pass rush, but the Blue Raiders — which entered the game with three sacks — landed five sacks on Delaware, and that pressure led to a safety and an interception. Cornerback Jackson Lowe has been the star of the defense, winning CUSA Defensive Player of the Week for his effort in Week 3. FIU (3-3, 1-1 CUSA) is a defensive juggernaut. The Panthers are tied for ninth nationally in scoring defense, allowing just 14.7 points per game. They are also ninth in total defense, 10th in third down defense, and first in opponent red zone touchdown percentage — giving up touchdowns on just 31.3 percent of opponent red zone trips. However, the Panthers don’t just force red zone struggles. They encounter them offensively, too. FIU is third in the CUSA in total offense yet ninth in scoring offense, and that can be attributed to what happens inside the 20-yard line. FIU’s red zone touchdown percentage of 31.8 percent is second-to-last in the FBS, scoring just seven touchdowns on 22 visits. item.content:encoded: Sep 26, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; Missouri State Bears quarterback Henry Belin IV (2) throws the ball during the second half against the SMU Mustangsat Gerald J. Ford Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cherish these Tuesday and Wednesday nights. We have two weeks of Weekday CUSA remaining before the conference hands the baton to Midweek MACtion in November. Last week, Weekday CUSA delivered with several thrillers. Three of the four games featured a go-ahead score in the final 3:30 of action, and these three were all decided by exactly three points. There are two double-digit spreads this week, but we’ve seen stranger things happen on Weekday CUSA in the past. Miami, Newark, Huntsville, and Kennesaw serve as the hosts as the four-game slate spans three nights this week. Middle Tennessee-FIU and Missouri State-Delaware are set for Tuesday. New Mexico State-Sam Houston is a standalone Wednesday night game. And Liberty-Kennesaw State concludes Week 8 of CUSA play on Thursday. Here is a preview of all four matchups: Middle Tennessee @ FIU Tuesday, Oct. 20 at 7 pm ET on CBS Sports Network Spread: FIU (-10) Over/under: 45.5 Middle Tennessee (3-3, 1-1 CUSA) has its best team in the three years of the Derek Mason era. The Blue Raiders have already matched their highest win total under Mason, and there are six games left on the regular season schedule. One reason for the Blue Raiders’ rapid ascension is the play of Roman Gagliano. The sophomore quarterback threw for 291 yards and three touchdowns last week to lead a back-and-forth win over Delaware. Gagliano has been complemented well by his receivers, including Cam’ron Lacy (369 yards, 4 TD), Markus Allen (176 yards, 1 TD), and Neo Clifton (166 yards, 3 TD). Middle Tennessee’s greatest weakness earlier in the season was its pass rush, but the Blue Raiders — which entered the game with three sacks — landed five sacks on Delaware, and that pressure led to a safety and an interception. Cornerback Jackson Lowe has been the star of the defense, winning CUSA Defensive Player of the Week for his effort in Week 3. FIU (3-3, 1-1 CUSA) is a defensive juggernaut. The Panthers are tied for ninth nationally in scoring defense, allowing just 14.7 points per game. They are also ninth in total defense, 10th in third down defense, and first in opponent red zone touchdown percentage — giving up touchdowns on just 31.3 percent of opponent red zone trips. However, the Panthers don’t just force red zone struggles. They encounter them offensively, too. FIU is third in the CUSA in total offense yet ninth in scoring offense, and that can be attributed to what happens inside the 20-yard line. FIU’s red zone touchdown percentage of 31.8 percent is second-to-last in the FBS, scoring just seven touchdowns on 22 visits. Quarterback JJ Kohl regularly slings it for over 250 yards, but his seven touchdowns have been matched by seven intereptions. Defensively, stars to monitor include defensive linemen Elisha Baldridge, Kenton Simmons, and DeeJay Holmes Jr. They have 3.0, 4.0, and 5.0 sacks, respectively, and 7.0, 6.0, 6.0 tackles for loss, respectively, as the architects behind FIU’s domineering defense. Prediction: FIU 19, Middle Tennessee 14 Missouri State @ Delaware Tuesday, Oct. 20 at 7 pm ET on ESPNU Spread: Delaware (-3) Over/under: 52.5 Missouri State (2-4, 1-1 CUSA) secured its first FBS win of the Casey Woods era last Wednesday, sliding past Kennesaw State on a 22-yard field goal from Yousef Obeid as time expired. The Bears fought hard against Marshall — and even SMU — but they finally finished the job in a close game. The offense is still looking for a spark, as the unit hasn’t registered more than 24 points in five contests against FBS teams. However, Missouri State flipped to Henry Belin IV at quarterback, and he excelled with 300 yards and two touchdowns in his first start since the 2023 TaxSlayer Bowl at Duke. Wide receiver Isaiah Myers has been dependable regardless of the quarterback, leading the CUSA with 554 receiving yards, and doing so on a 20.5 average. The Bears allow 30.5 points per game and are 126th in total defense, requiring progress in that facet. That improvement starts up front, as Missouri State ranks last in the conference in both sacks and tackles for loss. Nobody on the team has multiple sacks heading into Week 8. Delaware (2-4, 0-2 CUSA) had lofty expectations heading into the season but the Fightin’ Blue Hens remain winless in CUSA play. Delaware has dropped three straight, and that streak coincided with losing star quarterback Nick Minicucci to injury. The Fightin’ Blue Hens weren’t bad offensively in their Week 7 loss to Middle Tennessee, as true freshman Tyler Bell made his first start at quarterback and set a program freshman record with 306 passing yards. Nine different Hens caught a pass spanning at least 10 yards, showing the versatility of the receiving corps, which is usually led by Sean Wilson. However, especially without Minicucci, Delaware requires more run support, ranking fourth-to-last nationally with 94 rushing yards per game. The 125th-ranked pass defense could also use work, but Delaware has some capable backfield invaders. Linebackers Colin Gallagher and Blake Matthews combine for 82 tackles, 12.5 tackles for loss, and 8.0 sacks on the defense which produces the most sacks in the CUSA. Prediction: Delaware 26, Missouri State 24 New Mexico State @ Sam Houston Wednesday, Oct. 21 at 8 pm ET on ESPNU Spread: New Mexico State (-3) Over/under: 44.5 New Mexico State (2-4, 1-1 CUSA) must reinvigorate its offense. The Aggies enjoyed a stellar CUSA opener where they piled 34 points onto WKU, assisted by 155 rushing yards from lead back James Jones. However, New Mexico State hasn’t reached 20 points against its four other FBS opponents. Jones remains a force for the offense, ranking atop the conference with 599 rushing yards. The Aggies will need more from the passing game. Trey Hedden started the first four games at quarterback, while Adam Damante started the last two. They’ll need to ignite a versatile receiving corps led by the electric TK King (5’9”, 180) and complemented by AJ Williams III (6’4”, 195) and Brodie Malone-Bradford (6’5”, 205). Defensively, New Mexico State has been solid in CUSA play, only allowing two touchdowns across two games. The chaos is often created in the secondary. Strong safety Nick Session has 50 tackles and two interceptions, including a pick-six. Meanwhile, cornerback De’Marcus Peters has 21 stops and two defensive touchdowns — one from an interception and another from a fumble recovery. Sam Houston (1-5, 0-2 CUSA) looked like a dark-horse CUSA contender during non-conference play, falling just short of Troy and Tulsa, while giving Texas Tech all it could handle for a half. But since the start of that second half in Lubbock, the Bearkats have been unrecognizable from the team they were for most of September. Sam Houston hasn’t scored a touchdown in 10 quarters, notching just a field goal in each of its two conference losses against Liberty and WKU. Quarterback Landyn Locke remains the team’s greatest asset. He averaged 324 passing yards per game with nine touchdowns and one interceptions in his first three starts, but in his last three, he is averaging 148 with two touchdowns and three interceptions. The offensive line play must be better though, as the Bearkats are struggling to run and letting up the 13th-most sacks per game (2.83). Defensively, Sam Houston looks to create its first turnover in CUSA play. One candidate suited to lead the movement is 6’4” cornerback Ishmel Atkins, who ranks atop the team with five pass breakups. Prediction: New Mexico State 27, WKU 24 Liberty @ Kennesaw State Thursday, Oct. 22 at 7 pm ET on CBS Sports Network Spread: Liberty (-10.5) Over/under: 49.5 Liberty (5-1, 2-0 CUSA) is the clear-cut favorite to win the CUSA. The Flames lost by seven at undefeate

item.title: Sunderland officially hit rock bottom
item.description: Premier League Logo It is now official, Sunderland have hit rock bottom. Recent days have taken their toll. Sunderland losing 2-0 at Bournemouth on Sunday, a match where they could easily have lost by anything up to double figures as the Cherries wasted a ridiculous number of clear chances. The South coast team moving above the opposition in the Premier League table due to that result. That had followed Fulham’s narrow 1-0 victory on Saturday over Hull, the Craven Cottage side moving off rock bottom in the league. The weekend’s results meaning that if Tottenham avoided defeat on Monday night, Sunderland would end up 20th of 20 Premier League clubs. A 3-1 scoreline at home to Coventry City might suggest a comfortable Tottenham victory but it was anything but. Spurs twice took the lead with excellent finishes that were totally at odds with their general performance, then froze like rabbits in the headlights with zero confidence to then go on and make it a two or three goal margin victory. With such dismal form over such a long time, especially at home, Tottenham instead dropping off and inviting Coventry to attack. With a bit more quality and/or luck, Coventry would have got at least a point. Instead Spurs stumbled to the eventual win and a very late third goal that slowly went through the Coventry keeper’s hands gave an unrealistic look to the final scoreline. The stats backing up the idea that this was a far from convincing Tottenham victory, as Coventry had more touches of the ball in the opposition box (26 v 24), the same number of corners (4 each), a similar number of shots (16 Spurs v 12 Coventry), whilst the expected goals stats were only very marginally in Tottenham’s favour (0.87 v 0.82). The Premier League table is now beginning to take some shape. The seventh round of matches now completed and almost a fifth of the way through the league season. At the very top end you have three teams clear of the rest. Manchester City with a perfect seven wins and 21 points, whilst Arsenal aren’t looking great but scraping through game after game and have a record of six wins and one defeat for their 18 points. Then you have dark horses Brighton on 16 points and they are scoring for fun with 23 goals from seven EPL matches, the two teams above them having scored 19 (Man City) and 11 (Arsenal). These are the complete Premier League results from this seventh round of matches. Saturday 17 October Everton 0 Chelsea 2 Brentford 1 Liverpool 2 Fulham 1 Hull 0 Manchester City 3 Ipswich 2 Newcastle United 0 Aston Villa 1 Sunday 18 October Bournemouth 2 Sunderland 0 Brighton 5 Palace 0 Leeds 1 Man U 1 Forest 0 Arsenal 1 Monday 19 October Tottenham 3 Coventry 1 That leaves the Premier League table on Tuesday 20 October 2026 One of the stand out things for me is that only the top five and Ipswich have won more than two league matches so far, I think it is incredibly tight between so many teams. Pretty much any team can beat another, or draw. You can’t help though

item.title: Liverpool have found their next Xherdan Shaqiri in 22-goal star
item.description: Liverpool have found their next Xherdan Shaqiri in 22-goal star Liverpool have gone through a lot of changes over the last couple of years. The Reds' recruitment team have managed to spend well over £600 million on new players and, it's still unclear whether they're even any better off than they were before all that money was spent. Several areas among their ranks still need upgrading and, if they don't manage to do that, they're going to fall even further behind their title rivals. Obviously, this would be far from ideal, especially since they're now fifth in the Premier League table. To try and combat this, many transfers have been made and, now that we're a few months into the 2026-27 season, certain players are getting used to their surroundings with one of them even starting to remind fans of Xherdan Shaqiri . Victor Munoz could become Liverpool's new Xherdan Shaqiri Shaqiri was a bargain transfer that Liverpool completed back in 2018 when Stoke City were relegated. The Switzerland international only cost the Reds around £13.5 million and, while the transfer was questioned at the time, he managed to appear 63 times for Liverpool while contributing to 17 goals across all competitions. This may not seem like the best return but, when called upon, he always put in as much effort as possible and was often lauded by Jurgen Klopp . Since his departure, Liverpool have tried to replace him with the likes of Takumi Minamino and Federico Chiesa but, neither of them met expectations. But, this summer, Victor Munoz was brought in for the bargain price of £35 million and, even though he's a natural left-winger, his ability to play anywhere across the front three is just one of the many reasons why he's reminding fans of Shaqiri. The fact that he was brought in from a team who survive relegation to La Liga 2 thanks to goal difference is another similarity. But, the main thing is that, whenever he's been called upon thus far, he's always performed to a high standard and has easily managed to prove his worth. Victor Munoz could become an important player for Liverpool in the future Right now, Liverpool are still trying to figure out what their best XI is. But, since so many members of their squad are side-lined due to injury, it's been hard to Iraola to figure out who his usual starting XI should be. This has forced the Spaniard to try out many different players in many different positions and, of the lot, Munoz has probably been one of the most impressive. His outings for Liverpool have been second-to-none and, even though he may end up on the bench more often than he'd want to, there's still a massive chance for him to become an important player at Anfield. The Real Madrid academy graduate is only 23 years old so, even though he's already bagged himself two Premier League goals this season, there's every chance that he could become even better than he already is. Which, for the £35 million that Liverpool paid for him, would be unreal.

item.title: Davies ensures Spurs off the bottom after first win of season against Coventry
item.description: Tottenham are level with Beyoncé at last. Progress is represented in Roberto De Zerbi’s side earning only their sixth home win in the Premier League since November 2024. Cynics will point out that this spectacular stadium has hosted as many Beyoncé gigs during that time, but Spurs are finally singing a happier tune after dragging themselves out of the bottom three thanks to a messy but gritty 3-1 win over Coventry. It was not especially convincing. Coventry raged at the second Spurs goal, delivered when Omar Marmoush responded to Jack Rudoni’s equaliser for the visitors with a vicious effort in the 59th minute. Relief poured out of Marmoush after his first goal since joining on loan from Manchester City, but should it have stood? The Egyptian forward, who otherwise had a quiet game, was fortunate not to be penalised for an elbow on Milan van Ewijk. Continue reading...

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo receives 30-day suspension and £215 fine over Portugal walkout
item.description: Disciplinary council upholds charge against 41-year-old Fifa suspends Egypt’s Hossam Hassan and Mostafa Ziko Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended for 30 days by the Portuguese ⁠FA after leaving the national team camp following a rift with the coach, ⁠Jorge Jesus, over ⁠his role in the side. The federation’s disciplinary council said it had upheld the charge against ⁠the 41-year-old forward in full and imposed a fine of €255 (£215). Ronaldo left Portugal’s base in ⁠Copenhagen before their Nations League match against Denmark this month, having accused ‌Jesus of twice ‌breaking his word about his role after he was an ‌unused substitute against Norway. Jesus denied making any agreement with Ronaldo but left the door open for his return after Portugal’s 2-1 win. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Leaving England is scary but I’m here to win’: Charlie Cresswell on Ligue 1 life and his international dream
item.description: Young centre-back could not see a way forward at Leeds so moved to France. Now he’s preparing for the biggest game of his life against Juventus By Get French Football News “Leaving England is such a scary, scary decision,” says Charlie Cresswell. It is a decision that he never thought he would make. His father, Richard, made a career as a footballer in England; his brother, Alfie, was coming through Leeds’s academy; Charlie was on the fringes of the Leeds first team when the opportunity to join Toulouse arose in 2024. “That was the biggest decision I made in football,” he says. “I’ve been a Leeds fan since I was eight. I’d been at the club since I was 10, but, looking back, I was 20 years old with no games and I needed to get out and go play,” says Cresswell, now at Rennes and preparing to face Juventus in the Europa League. Continue reading...

item.title: Konsa bullish about Arsenal’s Champions League hopes as Bayern clash looms
item.description: Centre-back has settled right in at Arsenal and is looking ‘to win everything’, starting with Wednesday’s duel against Harry Kane For Ezri Konsa, it was just a wonderfully satisfying challenge. The Nottingham Forest striker Liam Delap had stolen in behind him up the inside left channel on Sunday. There were 93 minutes gone, Arsenal were 1-0 up and it was now or never for Forest. Konsa decreed that it would be never, curving his covering run back, matching Delap for pace and stretching into the perfect block tackle. So, another win for Arsenal : their 10th in 11 matches this season. Another clean sheet. And for Konsa, a continuation of what has been a dreamlike couple of months. Do points-saving last-minute challenges mean more when the defender is actually a fan of the club, too? Basically, yes. Continue reading...

item.title: Semenyo’s eight-week injury absence leaves Manchester City short on cover for Haaland
item.description: Ghana forward sustained knee injury against Ipswich Maresca to ring changes against AEK Athens on Tuesday Antoine Semenyo has been ruled out for eight weeks with a knee injury, leaving Enzo Maresca short of alternatives to Erling Haaland, who is a doubt for Manchester City’s Champions League game at home against AEK Athens on Tuesday. Semenyo limped off against Ipswich on Saturday and Haaland hobbled off at full time with a foot injury. City are eager to get their European campaign back on track after losing against Paris Saint-Germain last Wednesday. Maresca has said he will make changes and has admitted previously that Haaland will require resting at some point. Semenyo would have been the most obvious replacement but Phil Foden and Iliman Ndiaye could be utilised. Continue reading...
